source.title: A converse to a theorem of Gross, Zagier, and Kolyvagin
readSections: Read in full in the published version, the open-access PDF linked from the Annals article page for volume 191 (2020), issue 2, pages 329–354 (https://annals.math.princeton.edu/2020/191-2/p01), sha256 cfdfab6e62ac507be40d1f0bc8d9cb8371d95b42c5ae259fde054c70fb20c214, 26 pages, read 2026-09-23: §1 Introduction with Theorems A, A', B, C, D; §2 The proof of Theorem B (§2.1 Modular forms and abelian varieties, §2.2 Selmer groups, §2.3 More Galois cohomology, §2.4 The Heegner points P_K(f), §2.5 The Gross–Zagier theorem, §2.6 A p-adic L-function and a formal log of P_K(f), §2.7 Some Iwasawa theory for f and K, §2.8 An observation about hypothesis (irr_K), §2.9 Finishing the proof of Theorem B with Remark 2.9.1); §3 Theorem A follows from Theorem B; §4 A remark on the r = 0 case with Theorem E; and the references.

The arXiv preprint 1405.7294v1 (28 May 2014, 23 pages, sha256 of the PDF 9e4650618c83394c400a10e990759f9fba42113eedc79fe2fcbe029d6c8381ff; e-print archive sha256 80518dbef19f9dcf86686421f8c59c76af0bb1b2d6e69481b306d893162c0099, one file GZconverse-arxivready.tex of 1464 lines) was read alongside it for the exact LaTeX of every statement. It is the only arXiv version and predates publication by six years: the Annals page records Received 1 August 2013, Revised 1 December 2019, Accepted 2 December 2019, Published online 13 February 2020.

The two versions were compared statement by statement. The 19 numbered statements and their numbers agree exactly: Theorems A, A', B, C, D, E and Lemmas 2.2.1, 2.2.2, 2.3.1, 2.3.2, 2.8.1, Propositions 2.5.1, 2.6.1, 2.7.2, 2.7.3, Corollaries 2.5.2, 2.6.2, Conjecture 2.7.1, Remark 2.9.1. The one mathematical difference is in §§2.6–2.7 and is recorded as source issue E1: the published version places the anticyclotomic p-adic L-function in O^ur[[Γ]] and states Conjecture 2.7.1 and Proposition 2.7.2 as statements about ideals of Λ^ur ⊗_O L, where Λ = O[[Γ]] and Λ^ur = O^ur[[Γ]], whereas the preprint uses O[[Γ]] and Λ ⊗_{Z_p} Q_p throughout. The published text cites Wan Theorem 1.2 rather than part (2) of Theorem 1.1 of the older preprint. Its bibliography [26] still says 2014, to appear in Algebra Number Theory, arXiv:1408.4044; the prerequisite record supplies the eventual journal metadata (Algebra Number Theory 14 (2020), 383–483). Bhargava–Skinner and Brooks have published entries. Every item below states the published form.
The Annals article page lists no erratum or corrigendum for this paper, and arXiv has no version after v1.

Review REV-PAPER-SKINNER-20 (Claude Code, cc-39fac3, 23 September 2026): the published PDF (same SHA-256) read in full again, and arXiv 1405.7294v1 for E1; every item checked against the published text.

summary: Skinner’s squarefree-level rank-one and rank-zero converses, Theorem B with explicit Selmer injectivity and the mod-p Selmer criterion: 91 items (31 planned, 60 missing), eight routes with every missing item assigned exactly once. Restore the original A/E statements using the public Burungale–Skinner–Wan eigenlogarithm repair; request the general input at DT.3 and the RM/Heegner application at GZ.9. Add the shared elliptic Cassels–Tate inputs at SelmerIwasawaCohomology L1–L2, separate indefinite curve/transfer/quotient/normalization owners, and keep the A′ assembly in RankOneConverse. Twelve source issues retain the repaired historical omissions and the published/preprint distinctions.

items.name: The abelian variety A_f attached to a weight-two newform
items.statement: For a newform f ∈ S_2(Γ_0(N)) with trivial nebentypus, M_f ⊂ C is the field generated by the Hecke eigenvalues (the Fourier coefficients of the q-expansion at ∞), a totally real number field. The Eichler–Shimura construction attaches to f an abelian variety A_f over Q of dimension [M_f:Q], with End^0_Q(A_f) = M_f, characterised up to isogeny by L(A_f,s) = ∏_{σ: M_f ↪ C} L(f^σ,s), where f^σ is the newform whose q-expansion coefficients are the σ-images of those of f.
items.locator: §1, opening paragraphs, and §2.1, Skinner, Ann. of Math. (2) 191 (2020), 329–354
items.note: R14.5 plans the modular quotients J(X) → A_f with their endomorphism algebras, R29.5 the modular parametrisation and the L-function comparison, R19.1 the weight-two representation from the Jacobian with its coefficient field.

items.name: The theorem of Gross, Zagier and Kolyvagin
items.statement: Let r = 0 or 1. Then ord_{s=1}L(f,s) = r if and only if ord_{s=1}L(A_f,s) = [M_f:Q]·r, and ord_{s=1}L(f,s) = r implies rank_Z A_f(Q) = [M_f:Q]·r and #Ш(A_f) < ∞.
items.locator: §1, the displayed implication after the Birch–Swinnerton-Dyer conjecture, Skinner, Ann. of Math. (2) 191 (2020), 329–354 (Gross–Zagier; Kolyvagin; Kolyvagin–Logachev)
items.note: BSD.3 and BSD.4 plan the analytic-rank-one and analytic-rank-zero implications for elliptic curves, HE.7 the integral classical descent and full Sha finiteness, GZ.8 the height identity. The A_f statement with its factor [M_f:Q] is the Kolyvagin–Logachev form and is the same theorem at the level of each conjugate f^σ. Review note on status: Only partly planned. RankZeroOneBSD:BSD.3 and BSD.4 state the implication for elliptic curves E/Q only. The A_f form rests on HeegnerPointEulerSystems:HE.7's Kolyvagin–Logachev extension to RM quotients, and no stage assembles the A_f theorem with its factor [M_f:Q]. Keep it planned, citing HE.7 as the A_f owner, or add a note that the A_f assembly is missing.

items.name: The known converse in analytic rank zero
items.statement: (Skinner–Urban for N not squarefull; Wan for all N.) Let f ∈ S_2(Γ_0(N)) be a newform with trivial character. Suppose rank_Z A_f(Q) = 0 and Ш(A_f)[p^∞] is finite for a sufficiently large prime p such that f is ordinary with respect to some prime λ | p of M_f. Then ord_{s=1}L(f,s) = 0, so ord_{s=1}L(A_f,s) = 0. If A_f is a semistable elliptic curve, any prime p ≥ 11 of good ordinary reduction suffices.
items.locator: §1, the paragraph following the Gross–Zagier–Kolyvagin implication, Skinner, Ann. of Math. (2) 191 (2020), 329–354 (Skinner–Urban, Invent. Math. 195 (2014); Wan, thesis)
items.note: L1 plans the ordinary cyclotomic main conjecture in the Skinner–Urban form refined by Fouquet–Wan and L5 its arithmetic consequences; the rank-zero converse is the standard consequence of the Selmer-group side of that equality. Review (REV-PAPER-SKINNER-20): The statement never says what the converse is. It says only 'the converse holds: it suffices that ...'. Review note on status: This looks unplanned. ModularIwasawaMainConjectures:L1 plans the cyclotomic main conjecture, and L5 plans consequences such as Euler-factor changes and the Greenberg/Coates–Perrin-Riou conjectures, but neither states the rank-zero converse. Status should be missing, with L1 as its input. Review: status changed from planned to missing; ModularIwasawaMainConjectures L1 plans the ordinary main conjecture and L5 its consequences, but neither states the rank-zero converse (Skinner–Urban, Wan). Routed as a source of L5.

items.name: The rank-one converse for CM elliptic curves
items.statement: For r = 1 and A_f an elliptic curve with complex multiplication, the converse follows from Rubin's proof of the main conjecture for CM curves, Perrin-Riou's p-adic Gross–Zagier formula and Bertrand's non-degeneracy of the relevant p-adic height pairing; these are Theorems 8.1 and 8.2 of Rubin's paper. Since the theorems of the present paper assume N squarefree, A_f has no complex multiplication and the two sets of cases are disjoint.
items.locator: §1, the paragraph before Theorem A, and Remark 2.9.1(xii), Skinner, Ann. of Math. (2) 191 (2020), 329–354 (Rubin, Invent. Math. 107 (1992), Theorems 8.1, 8.2, 9.5)

items.name: Theorem A: the p-converse for A_f of squarefree level
items.statement: Let f ∈ S_2(Γ_0(N)) be a normalized weight-two cuspidal newform with trivial nebentypus, A_f/Q its modular abelian variety, M_f its totally real Hecke field, and π the cuspidal representation normalized by L(π,s−1/2)=L(f,s). Suppose N is squarefree and either an odd prime ℓ has π_ℓ equal to the twist of the special representation by the unique unramified quadratic character, or two distinct odd primes ℓ₁, ℓ₂ have π_{ℓ₁} and π_{ℓ₂} special. If rank_Z A_f(Q)=[M_f:Q] and Ш(A_f/Q) is finite, then ord_{s=1} L(f,s)=1.
items.locator: Theorem A (§1), with the Atkin–Lehner reformulation in the paragraph following it, Skinner, Ann. of Math. (2) 191 (2020), 329–354
items.note: The published Theorem A is retained under its original hypotheses. The historical omission in Lemma 2.2.2 is supplied by Burungale–Skinner–Wan (2026), Theorem 1.1, through items 81–82 and 20; E5 records that repair. No uniqueness of λ above p or extra logarithm assumption is imposed.

items.name: Theorem A': the p-converse for semistable elliptic curves
items.statement: Theorem A'. Let E be a semistable elliptic curve over Q. If there is at least one odd prime at which E has non-split multiplicative reduction, or at least two odd primes at which E has split multiplicative reduction, then rank_Z E(Q) = 1 and #Ш(E) < ∞ imply ord_{s=1}L(E,s) = 1. Since the hypotheses force the root number of E to be −1, the reduction hypotheses exclude only the semistable curves of conductor 2ℓ with ℓ an odd prime having split reduction at both 2 and ℓ.
items.locator: Theorem A' (§1) with the paragraph following it, Skinner, Ann. of Math. (2) 191 (2020), 329–354

items.name: Theorem B: the p-adic criterion over an imaginary quadratic field
items.statement: Theorem B. Suppose N is squarefree and p ≥ 5. Let K be an imaginary quadratic field with odd discriminant D. Suppose (a) p ∤ N and f is ordinary with respect to λ; (b) ρ̄_{f,λ} is irreducible and ramified at an odd prime that is either inert or ramified in K; (c) both 2 and p split in K; (d) if (D,N) ≠ 1 then for each ℓ | (D,N) the representation π_ℓ is the twist of the special representation by the unique unramified quadratic character, and each prime divisor of N/(D,N) splits in K; (e) dim_L H^1_f(K,V) = 1 and the restriction H^1_f(K,V) → ∏_{v|p}H^1_f(K_v,V) is an injection. Then ord_{s=1}L(f,K,s) = 1, rank_Z A_f(K) = [M_f:Q] = ord_{s=1}L(A_f/K,s), and Ш(A_f/K) is finite.
items.locator: Theorem B (§1), Skinner, Ann. of Math. (2) 191 (2020), 329–354

items.name: Theorem C: a mod-p Selmer criterion for semistable elliptic curves
items.statement: Theorem C. Let E be a semistable curve over Q such that there is at least one odd prime at which E has non-split multiplicative reduction or at least two odd primes at which E has split multiplicative reduction. Suppose there is a prime p ≥ 5 at which E has good ordinary reduction and such that (a) E[p] is an irreducible Gal(Q̄/Q)-representation; (b) Sel_p(E) ≅ Z/pZ; (c) the image of the restriction map Sel_p(E) → E(Q_p)/pE(Q_p) does not lie in the image of E(Q_p)[p]. Then ord_{s=1}L(E,s) = 1 = rank_Z E(Q) and #Ш(E) < ∞.
items.locator: Theorem C (§1), with its deduction sketched at the end of §3, Skinner, Ann. of Math. (2) 191 (2020), 329–354

items.name: Theorem D: a positive proportion of elliptic curves of rank one
items.statement: Theorem D (Bhargava–Skinner). When ordered by height, a positive proportion of elliptic curves has both algebraic and analytic rank one. It is through variations of Theorem B, of the kind exemplified by Theorem C, that Theorem B plays a crucial role in the proof of this statement.
items.locator: Theorem D (§1), Skinner, Ann. of Math. (2) 191 (2020), 329–354 (Bhargava–Skinner, J. Ramanujan Math. Soc. 29 (2014), 221–242)
items.note: ST.4 plans the Bhargava–Shankar orbit-counting Selmer theorems and their rank consequences and ST.5 the higher-moment and distribution refinements; the positive-proportion rank-one theorem is a consumer of those together with a p-converse of the kind proved here. Review note on status: This looks unplanned. ArithmeticStatistics:ST.4 plans the Bhargava–Shankar average-Selmer theorems and their rank bounds, and ST.5 plans higher moments. Neither plans the Bhargava–Skinner positive proportion of rank one, which also needs a p-converse and a parity/equidistribution input. Status should be missing, with ST.4 as an input. Review: status changed from planned to missing; ArithmeticStatistics ST.4 plans the Bhargava–Shankar Selmer averages and their rank bounds, not the Bhargava–Skinner positive proportion of rank one, which also needs a p-converse. Routed as a source of ST.4.

items.name: Theorem E: the analogous statement in analytic rank zero
items.statement: Let f ∈ S_2(Γ_0(N)) be a normalized weight-two cuspidal newform with trivial nebentypus, A_f/Q its modular abelian variety, M_f its totally real Hecke field, and π the cuspidal representation normalized by L(π,s−1/2)=L(f,s). Suppose N is squarefree and either an odd prime ℓ has π_ℓ equal to the twist of the special representation by the unique unramified quadratic character, or two distinct odd primes ℓ₁, ℓ₂ have π_{ℓ₁} and π_{ℓ₂} special. If A_f(Q) and Ш(A_f/Q) are both finite, then ord_{s=1} L(f,s)=0 (equivalently L(f,1)≠0).
items.locator: Theorem E (§4) with the proof sketch following it, Skinner, Ann. of Math. (2) 191 (2020), 329–354
items.note: The published Theorem E is retained. The logarithm input in its auxiliary-field proof is repaired by items 81–82 and 20. The separate derivative-nonvanishing input, item 76 and source issue E11, remains necessary; a root number alone does not supply it.

items.name: The strategy: from a non-vanishing p-adic L-value to a non-torsion Heegner point
items.statement: The proof of Theorem B runs: hypothesis (e) and the parity theorem give ε(f,K) = −1; the general Gross–Zagier formula then relates the Néron–Tate height of the Heegner point P_K(f) ∈ A_f(K) ⊗ M_f to L'(f,K,1), so it suffices to prove P_K(f) ≠ 0; the p-adic Gross–Zagier formula of Bertolini–Darmon–Prasanna and Brooks gives L^S_𝔭(f,1) ≐ (log_ω P_K(f))², so it suffices to prove L^S_𝔭(f,1) ≠ 0; and the Iwasawa–Greenberg main-conjecture divisibility of Wan gives the implication L^S_𝔭(f,1) = 0 ⟹ H^1_𝔭(K,V) ≠ 0, whose contrapositive applies because hypothesis (e) forces H^1_𝔭(K,V) = 0. The method is essentially p-adic but, unlike Rubin's CM proof, uses neither a p-adic Gross–Zagier formula for a derivative nor the non-degeneracy of a p-adic height.
items.locator: §1, the discussion between Theorem D and the acknowledgements, Skinner, Ann. of Math. (2) 191 (2020), 329–354

items.name: The λ-adic Galois representation V and its basic properties
items.statement: With T_pA_f the p-adic Tate module, V_pA_f = T_pA_f ⊗_{Z_p}Q_p, λ | p a prime of M_f, M_{f,p} = M_f ⊗ Q_p and L a finite extension of M_{f,λ}, set V = V_pA_f ⊗_{M_{f,p}}L. This is a two-dimensional L-space with a continuous L-linear G_Q-action ρ_{f,λ}, potentially semistable at p, unramified at ℓ ∤ Np, with V^∨ ≅ V(−1); for an embedding L ↪ C agreeing with M_f ↪ C one has L(V^∨,s) = L(f,s). The conventions for L-functions of potentially semistable representations are geometric: local Euler factors use characteristic polynomials of geometric Frobenius. The form f is ordinary with respect to λ if a_p(f) — the eigenvalue of T_p, or of U_p when p | N — is a unit in the ring of integers of L.
items.note: R19.1 constructs the weight-two representation with its coefficient field and lattices, R19.4 local–global compatibility away from p including the special case, R19.5 the potentially semistable and ordinary statements at p.

items.name: The K-twist of A_f and the factorisation of L(f,K,s)
items.statement: A_f^D is the twist of A_f by the cocycle in H^1(Q,Aut_Q A_f) given by the quadratic character χ_D of K, so that V_D = V_pA_f^D ⊗ L ≅ V ⊗ χ_D and L(A_f^D,s) = ∏_σ L(f^σ ⊗ χ_D,s); the natural map A_f × A_f^D → Res_{K/Q}A_f is a Q-isogeny whose kernel and cokernel are killed by 2. One sets L(f,K,s) = L(f,s)L(f ⊗ χ_D,s), whose sign of the functional equation is ε(f,K) = ε(f)ε(f ⊗ χ_D), and L(f,K,s) = L(BC_K(π),s−1/2) for the base change of π to GL_2(A_K).
items.note: Review note on status: In part planned. RankZeroOneBSD:BSD.0 plans the quadratic twist and the factorisation L(E/K,s) = L(E,s)L(E^K,s) for elliptic curves. The A_f twist and the isogeny A_f × A_f^D → Res_{K/Q}A_f are not planned.

items.name: The local root numbers of the base change and the sign ε(f,K)
items.statement: With ε_ℓ(π,K) = ∏_{𝔩|ℓ}ε(BC_{K_𝔩}(π_ℓ),1/2) one has ε(f,K) = ε(π,K) = −∏_ℓ ε_ℓ(π,K). If ℓ splits in K then ε_ℓ(π,K) = ε(π_ℓ,1/2)² = +1, so only primes inert or ramified in K contribute. If π_ℓ is the special representation σ_ℓ then ε_ℓ(π,K) = −1 when ℓ is inert or ramified, since there is a single prime 𝔩 above ℓ and BC_{K_𝔩}(σ_ℓ) is special. If π_ℓ = σ_ℓ ⊗ ξ_ℓ is the twist of the special representation by the unramified quadratic character, then ε_ℓ(π,K) = −1 when ℓ is inert (the base change is special) and +1 when ℓ is ramified (the base change is again a twist of the special representation by the unramified quadratic character). This uses that the root number of the special representation is −1 and that of its unramified quadratic twist is +1.
items.locator: §2.1, the final paragraph, Skinner, Ann. of Math. (2) 191 (2020), 329–354 (Kramer–Tunnell; Jacquet–Langlands, Propositions 3.5 and 3.6)
items.note: R16.3 plans local Langlands for GL₂ with the special representations and their ε-factors, R17.4 cyclic base change, AL.2 the local L- and ε-factors; the computation here is their combination for a quadratic base change.

items.name: Bloch–Kato Selmer groups of V and the vanishing away from p
items.statement: H^1_f(K,V) = ker{H^1(K,V) → ∏_𝔩 H^1(K_𝔩,V)/H^1_f(K_𝔩,V)}, where H^1_f(K_𝔩,V) = ker{H^1(K_𝔩,V) → H^1(K_𝔩,B_cris ⊗ V)} for 𝔩 | p and H^1_f(K_𝔩,V) = H^1(F_𝔩,V^{I_𝔩}) for 𝔩 ∤ p. By Tate's local Euler characteristic formula, local duality and V ≅ V^∨(1), dim H^1(K_𝔩,V) = 2 dim H^0(K_𝔩,V) for 𝔩 ∤ p, and local–global compatibility gives V^{G_{K_𝔩}} = 0, so H^1_f(K_𝔩,V) = H^1(K_𝔩,V) = 0. Hence for any finite S containing the primes dividing pN, H^1_f(K,V) = ker{H^1(G_{K,S},V) → ∏_{𝔩|p}H^1(K_𝔩,V)/H^1_f(K_𝔩,V)}.
items.locator: §2.2, Skinner, Ann. of Math. (2) 191 (2020), 329–354 (Bloch–Kato; Fontaine–Perrin-Riou; the vanishing cf. Nekovář–Plater, Lemma 3.1.3)
items.note: L2 plans the local conditions and the Selmer group as the kernel of the global-to-local map, L4 the finite Bloch–Kato condition once period rings are available, and L1 the local duality and Euler-characteristic input.

items.name: Decomposition of the Selmer group under Gal(K/Q)
items.statement: Restriction from G_Q to G_K induces an isomorphism H^1_f(Q,V) ⊕ H^1_f(Q,V_D) ≅ H^1_f(K,V), and the left-hand side is the decomposition of the right-hand side into the subspaces on which Gal(K/Q) acts trivially and non-trivially.
items.locator: §2.2, the display before Lemma 2.2.1, Skinner, Ann. of Math. (2) 191 (2020), 329–354

items.name: Lemma 2.2.1: odd Selmer dimension forces sign −1
items.statement: Lemma 2.2.1. Suppose p ∤ ND and f is ordinary with respect to λ | p. If dim_L H^1_f(K,V) is odd, then ε(f,K) = −1. (Proof: the dimension is dim H^1_f(Q,V) + dim H^1_f(Q,V_D); one summand is odd and the other even, so by the parity theorem for Selmer groups of λ-ordinary modular forms one of ε(f) and ε(f ⊗ χ_D) is −1 and the other +1.)
items.locator: Lemma 2.2.1, Skinner, Ann. of Math. (2) 191 (2020), 329–354

items.name: Nekovář's parity theorem for Selmer groups of ordinary modular forms
items.statement: (Nekovář, Selmer Complexes, Th. 12.2.3, in the form used here.) Let f ∈ S_2(Γ_0(N)) be a newform with trivial character, p an odd prime with p ∤ N, and λ | p a prime of M_f at which f is ordinary. Let V be the λ-adic representation of §2.1. Then (−1)^{dim_L H^1_f(Q,V)} = ε(f). The paper applies this to f and to f ⊗ χ_D, which is also λ-ordinary because p ∤ D gives a_p(f⊗χ_D) = χ_D(p)a_p(f).
items.locator: Used in Lemma 2.2.1 and again in §3, Skinner, Ann. of Math. (2) 191 (2020), 329–354 (Nekovář, Selmer complexes, Astérisque 310 (2006), Theorem 12.2.3)
items.note: Review (REV-PAPER-SKINNER-20): The statement is garbled ('For a newform f ... and a quadratic twist') and omits the hypotheses under which the theorem is applied.

items.name: The p-power Selmer group of A_f and its relation to H^1_f(K,V)
items.statement: Let A_f, p, K and V be as in §2.1, T_pA_f its Tate module and W=V_pA_f/T_pA_f≅A_f[p^∞]. Put Ш(A_f/K)=ker(H¹(K,A_f(K̄))→∏_v H¹(K_v,A_f(K̄_v))) and Sel_{p^∞}(A_f/K)=ker(H¹(K,W)→∏_v H¹(K_v,A_f(K̄_v))). For each place v let H¹_f(K_v,W) be the image of the local Kummer map A_f(K_v)⊗Q_p/Z_p→H¹(K_v,W); it is also the image of the Bloch–Kato subgroup H¹_f(K_v,V_pA_f). At v∤p the groups H¹(K_v,V_pA_f), H¹_f(K_v,V_pA_f) and H¹_f(K_v,W) vanish in this setting. There is an exact sequence 0→A_f(K)⊗Q_p/Z_p→Sel_{p^∞}(A_f/K)→Ш(A_f/K)[p^∞]→0. For finite S containing the primes above pN, Sel_{p^∞} lies in H¹(G_{K,S},W) and is cut out by restriction into H¹_f(K_v,W) for v∈S. The image of H¹(G_{K,S},V_pA_f) in H¹(G_{K,S},W) is the maximal divisible subgroup and has finite index. The maximal divisible subgroup of Sel_{p^∞} is the image of H¹_f(K,V_pA_f). The rational Kummer injection A_f(K)⊗Q_p→H¹_f(K,V_pA_f) has cokernel dimension equal to corank_{Z_p} Ш(A_f/K)[p^∞]. Writing M_{f,p}=M_f⊗Q_p and L=M_{f,λ} (or a finite extension), H¹_f(K,V)=H¹_f(K,V_pA_f)⊗_{M_{f,p}}L and H¹_f(K_v,V)=H¹_f(K_v,V_pA_f)⊗_{M_{f,p}}L.
items.locator: §2.2, 'Connections with the Selmer group of A_f', Skinner, Ann. of Math. (2) 191 (2020), 329–354
items.note: Restores the complete §2.2 contract. SelmerIwasawaCohomology L2 supplies lattice/divisible local conditions and L4 the Bloch–Kato/Kummer comparison. The vanishing concerns the three named local groups, not all of H¹(K_v,W). No finiteness of Ш is assumed in these definitions or the exact sequence.

items.name: Lemma 2.2.2: rank one and finite Sha give hypothesis (e)
items.statement: Let f, A_f, M_f, p, λ, L and V be as in §2.1, and K the imaginary quadratic field of the paper. If rank_Z A_f(K)=[M_f:Q] and Ш(A_f/K)[p^∞] is finite, then dim_L H¹_f(K,V)=1 and restriction H¹_f(K,V)→H¹(K_v,V) is injective for every v|p. The same assertion holds with K replaced by Q.
items.locator: Lemma 2.2.2, Skinner, Ann. of Math. (2) 191 (2020), 329–354
items.note: Published Lemma 2.2.2, with its Q-specialization used in §3. By item 19 the global space is the λ-component of the rank-one M_f-module A_f(K)⊗Q. Choose an actual non-torsion point spanning this module after clearing denominators. Item 81 makes its logarithm nonzero in every eigencomponent, for every embedding at v|p; the Kummer/logarithm comparison of item 77 then makes restriction injective on the one-dimensional L-space. This repairs E5 without a restriction on the number of primes above p.

items.name: The strict Selmer group and the Selmer groups H^1_𝔭, H^1_𝔭̄ (strict at one prime above p, relaxed at the other)
items.statement: For S containing the primes dividing pN, H^i(K_p,V) = ∏_{𝔩|p}H^i(K_𝔩,V) and H^1_str(K,V) = ker{H^1(G_{K,S},V) → H^1(K_p,V)}, independent of S. When p = 𝔭𝔭̄ splits in K, H^1_𝔭(K,V) = ker{H^1(G_{K,S},V) → H^1(K_𝔭,V)} and H^1_{𝔭̄}(K,V) is defined likewise; both are independent of S.
items.note: Review (REV-PAPER-SKINNER-20): The name is wrong. H^1_𝔭(K,V) = ker{H^1(G_{K,S},V) → H^1(K_𝔭,V)} is strict at 𝔭 and relaxed at 𝔭̄, not '𝔭-relaxed'. The intro calls it the subspace of classes vanishing at all w ≠ 𝔭̄. The statement itself is correct. Review note on status: Looks planned. SelmerIwasawaCohomology:L2 defines unramified, strict, relaxed and Greenberg local conditions separately. Review: status changed from missing to planned; SelmerIwasawaCohomology L2 defines 'unramified, strict, relaxed and Greenberg conditions separately' and the Selmer groups they cut out, of which these are instances.

items.name: Lemma 2.3.1: the semilocal image at p is two-dimensional
items.statement: Lemma 2.3.1. dim_L im{H^1(G_{K,S},V) → H^1(K_p,V)} = 2. (Proof: by Tate global duality H^1_str(K,V) is dual to H^2(G_{K,S},V), using H^1(K_𝔩,V) = 0 for 𝔩 ∤ p and H^2(K_𝔩,V) = 0 for all 𝔩; then the global Euler characteristic formula and H^0(G_{K,S},V) = 0 give the difference of dimensions 2.)
items.locator: Lemma 2.3.1, Skinner, Ann. of Math. (2) 191 (2020), 329–354

items.name: Tate global duality and the global Euler characteristic formula
items.statement: Let K be a number field, S a finite set of places containing those above p and ∞, and V a finite-dimensional continuous L-representation of G_{K,S}. (Poitou–Tate) For i = 1, 2, Ш^i_S(V) := ker(H^i(G_{K,S},V) → ⊕_{v∈S}H^i(K_v,V)) is L-dual to Ш^{3−i}_S(V^∨(1)). (Tate) Σ_i(−1)^i dim_L H^i(G_{K,S},V) = Σ_{v|∞} dim_L H^0(K_v,V) − [K:Q]·dim_L V. (Local) For v ∤ p finite, dim H^1(K_v,V) = dim H^0(K_v,V) + dim H^2(K_v,V), and H^2(K_v,V) is dual to H^0(K_v,V^∨(1)). In §2.3, with K imaginary quadratic, V ≅ V^∨(1), H^1(K_𝔩,V) = 0 for 𝔩 ∤ p and H^2(K_𝔩,V) = 0 for all 𝔩, these give H^1_str(K,V) = Ш^1_S(V) dual to H^2(G_{K,S},V) = Ш^2_S(V), and dim H^1 − dim H^2 = 2.
items.locator: §2.2 (local Euler characteristic and local duality, p. 336) and Lemma 2.3.1 with its proof (p. 338)
items.note: R02.4 plans Poitou–Tate duality and R02.3 global finiteness and the Euler characteristic; L1 their Selmer-theoretic application. Review (REV-PAPER-SKINNER-20): As a general statement this is false: for an arbitrary p-adic V the strict Selmer group is not dual to H^2(G_{K,S},V). Poitou–Tate pairs Ш^1_S(V^∨(1)) with Ш^2_S(V), and the identification needs H^1(K_𝔩,V) = 0 for 𝔩 ∤ p, H^2(K_𝔩,V) = 0 and V ≅ V^∨(1). Also, the Euler-characteristic inputs are used in §2.2 (the vanishing of H^1(K_𝔩,V) for 𝔩 ∤ p) and in Lemma 2.3.1, not in Lemma 2.2.1.

items.name: Lemma 2.3.2: one-dimensional image at p kills H^1_𝔭, H^1_str and H^1_𝔭̄
items.statement: Lemma 2.3.2. If dim_L im{H^1_f(K,V) → H^1_f(K_p,V)} = 1, then H^1_𝔭(K,V) = H^1_str(K,V) = H^1_{𝔭̄}(K,V). If in addition dim_L H^1_f(K,V) = 1, then all three vanish. (Proof: X, the image of H^1(G_{K,S},V) in H^1(K_p,V), is two-dimensional by Lemma 2.3.1; complex conjugation swaps the images X_𝔭 and X_{𝔭̄}; if X_𝔭 ≠ 0 then X = X_𝔭 ⊕ X_{𝔭̄} = X^+ ⊕ X^-, the one-dimensional c-stable X_f equals X^+ or X^-, whence X_𝔭 ⊂ H^1_f(K_{𝔭̄},V) and X_{𝔭̄} ⊂ H^1_f(K_𝔭,V), making X_f two-dimensional, a contradiction.)
items.locator: Lemma 2.3.2, Skinner, Ann. of Math. (2) 191 (2020), 329–354
items.note: Review (REV-PAPER-SKINNER-20): The name repeats the '𝔭-relaxed' error of item 21. H^1_𝔭 is 𝔭-strict. The statement is correct.

items.name: The two cases for the pair (f,K)
items.statement: Case I: every prime ℓ | N either splits or ramifies in K. Case II: N = N^-N^+ with N^- a non-trivial product of an even number of primes inert in K and N^+ a product of primes that split in K (so (D,N) = 1). Under (sqf), (sgn) and (ram) the pair (f,K) is in Case I or Case II.
items.locator: §2.4, the two displayed cases, and §2.5, Skinner, Ann. of Math. (2) 191 (2020), 329–354

items.name: The Heegner point P_K(f) in Case I
items.statement: Let T be the Hecke algebra generated over Z by the T_ℓ, ℓ ∤ N, acting on S_2(Γ_0(N)), T_{M_f} = T ⊗ M_f, ε_f ∈ T_{M_f} the idempotent projecting to the f-eigenvalue system, 𝔭_f = ker ε_f|_T, X = X_0(N), ω_f the differential pulling back to 2πi f(τ)dτ, A_f = J(X)/𝔭_fJ(X) with quotient map φ, and ω ∈ Ω^1(A_f) ⊗ M_f the form with φ^*ω = ω_f. Let 𝔫 ⊂ O_K have norm N — possible because every ℓ | N splits or ramifies in K — so that C/O_K → C/𝔫^{-1} is a cyclic N-isogeny of CM elliptic curves and defines P ∈ X(H) over the Hilbert class field. With D_K = Σ_{σ ∈ Gal(H/K)}P^σ and D_{K,ℓ} = (T_ℓ − 1 − ℓ)·D_K ∈ Div^0(X), set Q_K(f) = (a_ℓ(f) − 1 − ℓ)^{-1}ε_f·[D_{K,ℓ}] ∈ J(X)(K) ⊗ M_f, independent of ℓ, and P_K(f) = φ(Q_K(f)) ∈ A_f(K) ⊗ M_f.
items.locator: §2.4, Case I, Skinner, Ann. of Math. (2) 191 (2020), 329–354
items.note: HE.0 plans ring class fields and reciprocity, HE.1 the CM points on X_0(N) and their descent to the ring class field together with the map to A_f through the modular quotient and the normalised Hodge class, CM.3 the Hilbert class field. The ε_f-normalisation over M_f is the only addition, recorded as PAPER-SKINNER-20/27. Review note on status: The note refers to 'PAPER-SKINNER-20/27', which is not an item id in this extraction. It presumably means PAPER-SKINNER-20/27.

items.name: Comparison of the normalisations of the Heegner divisor
items.statement: With D^0_K = D_K − #Gal(H/K)·∞ and Q^0_K = [D^0_K] ∈ J(X)(K), and with ξ the normalised degree-one Hodge divisor of Yuan–Zhang–Zhang, D^ξ_K = D_K − #Gal(H/K)·ξ and Q^ξ_K = [D^ξ_K] ∈ J(X)(K) ⊗ Q, one has ε_f·Q^0_K = Q_K(f) = ε_f·Q^ξ_K, because the cusps are Eisenstein (T_ℓ·∞ = (1+ℓ)·∞) and, by the expression for the Hodge divisor in terms of the canonical divisor, ξ is Eisenstein as well. The Hodge-class identity ε_f·Q^ξ_K=Q_K(f) also holds in Case II; the cusp construction is only for Case I.
items.locator: §2.4, the paragraph on comparison with other constructions, Skinner, Ann. of Math. (2) 191 (2020), 329–354 (Yuan–Zhang–Zhang, §§1.2.2, 3.1.3)

items.name: The Heegner point P_K(f) in Case II
items.statement: In Case II, X is the Shimura curve over Q attached to the indefinite quaternion algebra B of discriminant N^- and an Eichler order O_{B,N^+} of level N^+ in a maximal order O_B, with an embedding K ↪ B such that K ∩ O_{B,N^+} = O_K. Replacing f by its Jacquet–Langlands transfer f_B, normalised as in Skinner’s citation of Brooks §2.8 (published Brooks §2.7 for the transfer normalization; see E12) to be defined over M_f, and 𝔫 by an integral ideal 𝔫^+ of K of norm N^+, the constructions of Case I yield Q_K(f) = Q_K(f_B) ∈ J(X)(K) ⊗ M_f and P_K(f) = P_K(f_B) ∈ A_f(K) ⊗ M_f, and Q^ξ_K with ε_f·Q^ξ_K = Q_K(f).
items.locator: §2.4, Case II, Skinner, Ann. of Math. (2) 191 (2020), 329–354
items.note: Import the quaternionic CM points, rational Hodge class, denominator tracking and image under the modular quotient from HeegnerPointEulerSystems:HE.1. This missing item in RankOneConverse is the Skinner-specific ε_f normalization and its comparison with Brooks, through items 68 and 87–90; it is not a second construction of the curve or general CM points.

items.name: The hypotheses (sqf), (sgn) and (ram)
items.statement: (sqf): N is squarefree. (sgn): ε(f,K) = −1. (ram): if (D,N) ≠ 1 then π_ℓ ≅ σ_ℓ ⊗ ξ_ℓ for each ℓ | (D,N) and each ℓ | N/(D,N) splits in K. Since the central character of π is trivial, (sqf) implies that for each ℓ | N the local component π_ℓ is either the special representation σ_ℓ or its unramified quadratic twist σ_ℓ ⊗ ξ_ℓ; (sgn) implies that the number of ℓ | N with ε_ℓ(π,K) = −1 is even, so when (D,N) = 1 the number of prime divisors of N inert in K is even.
items.locator: §2.5, the displayed hypotheses, Skinner, Ann. of Math. (2) 191 (2020), 329–354

items.name: Proposition 2.5.1: Gross–Zagier for the Heegner point of f
items.statement: Proposition 2.5.1 (Yuan–Zhang–Zhang). Suppose (sqf), (sgn) and (ram) hold. If P_K(f) ≠ 0 then ord_{s=1}L(f,K,s) = 1. The proof identifies P_K(f) = h_K·P(f_1)^ι with h_K = #Gal(H/K) and, for a symmetric ample line bundle 𝓛 with polarisation λ, computes ⟨P_K(f),P_K(f)⟩_𝓛 = ⟨P_K(f),λ(P_K(f))⟩_{NT} = h_K²ζ(2)L'(f,K,1)(f_1∘f_2^∨)^ι / (4L(χ_D,1)²L(Sym²f,2)vol(X)) by Yuan–Zhang–Zhang Theorem 3.13, so that P_K(f) ≠ 0 if and only if the height is non-zero.
items.locator: Proposition 2.5.1 with the computation following it, Skinner, Ann. of Math. (2) 191 (2020), 329–354 (Yuan–Zhang–Zhang, The Gross–Zagier Formula on Shimura Curves, Theorem 3.13 and §3.2.5)
items.note: GZ.8 plans the general Gross–Zagier pairing for factorisable test vectors in the quaternionic realisation, GZ.3 the rational automorphic realisations and the pairing of f_1 with f_2^∨, GZ.0 the normalisation conventions including the choice of line bundle and the zeta/eta factors.

items.name: Corollary 2.5.2: the order of vanishing of L(A_f/K,s)
items.statement: Corollary 2.5.2. If P_K(f) ≠ 0 then ord_{s=1}L(A_f/K,s) = [M_f:Q]. (If P_K(f) = ΣP ⊗ r_P with P running over a basis of A_f(K) ⊗ Q and r_P ∈ M_f, then P_K(f^σ) = ΣP ⊗ σ(r_P) for every σ : M_f ↪ R, so P_K(f) ≠ 0 if and only if P_K(f^σ) ≠ 0 for all σ; Proposition 2.5.1 applied to every conjugate then gives the corollary.)
items.locator: Corollary 2.5.2 with the paragraph preceding it, Skinner, Ann. of Math. (2) 191 (2020), 329–354

items.name: The anticyclotomic tower and its Hodge–Tate characters
items.statement: K_∞/K is the anticyclotomic Z_p-extension, Γ = Gal(K_∞/K) ≅ Z_p with conjugation by c inverting Γ, and Ψ : G_K ↠ Γ the canonical projection; p = 𝔭𝔭̄ splits in K, λ is the prime of M_f determined by the fixed embedding Q̄ ↪ K̄_𝔭, and an embedding K̄_𝔭 ↪ C is fixed compatibly. A continuous ψ : Γ → Q_p^× is Hodge–Tate if it is so as a representation of G_{K_𝔭} or, equivalently by anticyclotomicity, of G_{K_{𝔭̄}}; the weights are then (−n,n) for an integer n, and ψ is the p-adic avatar of a unitary algebraic Hecke character ψ^alg of infinity type z^n z̄^{-n}, given by ψ^alg((x_v)) = x_𝔭^{-n}x_{𝔭̄}^{n}x_∞^{n}x̄_∞^{-n}·ψ∘rec_K((x_v)) with rec_K normalised so that uniformisers correspond to geometric Frobenius, whence L(ψ^alg,s) = L(ψ,s). Σ^c_𝔭 is the set of crystalline ψ of weight (−n,n) with n > 0 and n ≡ 0 mod p−1; crystallinity is equivalent to ψ^alg being unramified at 𝔭 and 𝔭̄.
items.note: L0 plans locally algebraic Hecke characters, their p-adic avatars through chosen embeddings, infinity types and the ray-class character space; L3 the Z_p-extension and its Iwasawa algebra; CM.4 the CM Hecke character/Galois dictionary.

items.name: The hypotheses (flt), (odd) and (L-lrg)
items.statement: (flt): p ∤ N. (odd): D is odd. (L-lrg): L contains a large enough finite extension of Q_p — it is enough that L contain the image of the Hilbert class field of K.
items.locator: §2.6, the displayed hypotheses, Skinner, Ann. of Math. (2) 191 (2020), 329–354

items.name: The anticyclotomic p-adic L-function and its interpolation
items.statement: Assume (sqf), (sgn), (ram), (flt), (odd), (L-lrg), let S = {ℓ | pND}, O the ring of integers of L and O^ur that of the completion of the maximal unramified extension L^ur of L. There is an anticyclotomic p-adic L-function L^S_𝔭(f) ∈ O^ur[[Γ]] such that for ψ ∈ Σ^c_𝔭, ψ(L^S_𝔭(f)) = C(f,K)w(f,ψ)e_∞(f,ψ)e_p(f,ψ)Ω_p(ψ)·L^S(f,ψ^alg,1)/Ω(ψ^alg), where L^S(f,ψ^alg,s) = L^S(V^∨ ⊗ ψ,s) omits the Euler factors at the primes of K above S; Ω(ψ^alg) = (2πi)^{-2n-1}(2π)^{1-2n}Ω^{4n}D^{n-1/2} with Ω a period of an elliptic curve E_0 with CM by O_K; Ω_p(ψ) = Ω_p^{4n}; e_∞(f,ψ) = 4(2π)^{-2n-1}Γ(n)Γ(n+1); e_p(f,ψ) = (1 − a_p(f)ψ^alg(𝔭̄)p^{-1} + ψ^alg(𝔭̄)²p^{-1})/(1 − a_p(f)ψ^alg(𝔭)p^{-1} + ψ^alg(𝔭)²p^{-1}); w(f,ψ) = ψ(W) for a unit W ∈ O^ur[[Γ]]^× with w(f,1) = w_K; and C(f,K) a non-zero constant depending on f and K. One writes L^S_𝔭(f,ψ) = ψ(L^S_𝔭(f)).
items.locator: §2.6, the displayed interpolation formula, Skinner, Ann. of Math. (2) 191 (2020), 329–354 (Bertolini–Darmon–Prasanna; Brooks; Brakočević; Eischen–Harris–Li–Skinner; Wan)
items.note: GZ.9 plans the construction of the BDP/Brooks p-adic L-function in the weight-two Heegner setting at a prime split in the imaginary quadratic field, with its actual interpolation range, CM periods and removed Euler factors, in both the modular-curve and the quaternionic case.

items.name: The p-adic L-function belongs to the Iwasawa algebra
items.statement: The functions constructed in Bertolini–Darmon–Prasanna and in Brooks are a priori only continuous on Γ. That L^S_𝔭(f) belongs to the Iwasawa algebra O^ur[[Γ]] requires an additional argument, essentially the extension of the interpolation formulas to characters ramified at the primes above p, as carried out by Brakočević; it also follows from the constructions of Eischen–Harris–Li–Skinner and of Wan, and, when some ℓ | N is inert or ramified in K, the function is constructed directly in those two references. It can be related to a specialisation of Hida's three-variable Rankin–Selberg p-adic L-function.
items.locator: §2.6, the paragraph after the interpolation formula, Skinner, Ann. of Math. (2) 191 (2020), 329–354 (Brakočević, IMRN 2011; Eischen–Harris–Li–Skinner; Wan, Algebra Number Theory 14 (2020); Hida, Ann. Inst. Fourier 38 (1988))
items.note: Review note on status: Possibly planned. GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.9 constructs the BDP/Brooks function using PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras measures. If that construction is an element of the Iwasawa algebra, mark this item planned at GZ.9. Otherwise the Brakočević extension to characters ramified at p is missing.

items.name: Identification with the BDP and Brooks p-adic L-functions
items.statement: For ψ ∈ Σ^c_𝔭 let χ be the Hecke character with χ^{-1} = ψ^alg|Nm(·)|_Q. Then L^S_𝔭(f) is the imprimitive variant — the Euler factors at the primes of S not dividing p removed — of the p-adic L-function denoted L_p(f,χ) in Bertolini–Darmon–Prasanna (Case I) and in Brooks (Case II); the corresponding set of χ is Σ^{(2)}_{cc}(𝔫), respectively Σ^{(2)}_{cc}(𝔫^+), and the interpolated values are given there in terms of L(f,χ^{-1},0) = L(f,ψ^alg,1). In that notation e_∞(f,ψ)w_K(2πi)^{1+2n} = C(f,χ,1), w(f,ψ) = w_K w(f,χ)^{-1}, and C(f,K) is the constant α(f,f_{GL_2})^{-1} of Brooks.
items.locator: §2.6, the paragraph beginning 'For ψ ∈ Σ^c_𝔭', Skinner, Ann. of Math. (2) 191 (2020), 329–354
items.note: Review note on status: Arguably planned at GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.9, which constructs BDP/Brooks with their removed Euler factors and CM periods in both the modular-curve and quaternionic cases.

items.name: Proposition 2.6.1: the p-adic Gross–Zagier formula at the BDP point
items.statement: Proposition 2.6.1 (Bertolini–Darmon–Prasanna; Brooks). Suppose (sqf), (sgn), (ram), (flt) and (odd) hold. Then L^S_𝔭(f,1) ≐ (log_ω P_K(f))², where ≐ is equality up to a non-zero constant depending also on the eigenvalues at the primes in S, ω ∈ Ω^1(A_f) ⊗ M_f satisfies φ^*ω = ω_f, and log_ω : A_f(K_𝔭) ⊗ L → K̄_𝔭 is the formal logarithm determined by ω. The trivial character ψ = 1, the BDP point, is not in Σ^c_𝔭.
items.locator: Proposition 2.6.1, Skinner, Ann. of Math. (2) 191 (2020), 329–354 (Bertolini–Darmon–Prasanna, Pacific J. Math. 260 (2012), Theorem 3.12; Brooks, IMRN 2015, Proposition 8.13)
items.note: GZ.9 plans the p-adic Waldspurger identity at the weight-two point outside the interpolation range — the specified specialisation equals the square of the formal logarithm of the corresponding Heegner point times explicit local factors — including the quaternionic variant of Brooks Proposition 8.13.

items.name: Reduction of Proposition 2.6.1 to the published formulas
items.statement: In Case I, Proposition 2.6.1 is BDP [1, Th. 3.12], whose formula has log_ω P_f with P_f = φ(Q^0_K). Since φ^*ω = ω_f we have log_ω P_f = log_{ω_f}Q^0_K. Since ε_f·ω_f = ω_f, log_{ω_f}Q^0_K = log_{ω_f}ε_f·Q^0_K = log_{ω_f}Q_K(f) = log_ω P_K(f), which gives the stated form. In Case II the proposition follows in the same way from Brooks Proposition 8.13.
items.locator: §2.6, the paragraph after Proposition 2.6.1, Skinner, Ann. of Math. (2) 191 (2020), 329–354
items.note: Review (REV-PAPER-SKINNER-20): This copies a misprint: the printed 'log_ω P_K = log_{ω_f} Q^0_K' should read 'log_ω P_f = log_{ω_f} Q^0_K', since P_f = φ(Q^0_K) and φ^*ω = ω_f (new issue PAPER-SKINNER-20/new-3). Review note on status: Arguably planned at GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.9, which includes the exact differential normalisation and Brooks Prop. 8.13.

items.name: Corollary 2.6.2: non-vanishing of the Heegner point is non-vanishing of the p-adic L-value
items.statement: Let f be as in §2.1 and K an imaginary quadratic field of odd discriminant D. Assume N is squarefree, ε(f,K)=−1, p∤N and p=𝔭𝔭̄ splits in K. If (D,N)≠1, assume π_ℓ is the unramified quadratic twist of the special representation for every ℓ|(D,N), and every prime dividing N/(D,N) splits in K. With the normalized Heegner point and imprimitive p-adic L-function of §§2.4–2.6 (coefficient field enlarged as needed), P_K(f)≠0 if and only if L^S_𝔭(f,1)≠0, where S={ℓ:ℓ|pND}.
items.locator: Corollary 2.6.2, Skinner, Ann. of Math. (2) 191 (2020), 329–354
items.note: Restores Corollary 2.6.2. Proposition 2.6.1 supplies the equivalence between the L-value and the squared logarithm. Item 82 proves nonvanishing of that logarithm for this projected rational divisor point, using item 81; it is not an assertion about arbitrary nonzero tensors or cohomology classes. Only L-value nonzero ⇒ point nonzero is needed for Theorem B.

items.name: The big Galois module M and the Iwasawa–Greenberg Selmer group
items.statement: Let O be the ring of integers of L, T ⊂ V a G_Q-stable O-lattice, Λ = O[[Γ]] and Λ^ur = O^ur[[Γ]] with O^ur the ring of integers of the completion of the maximal unramified extension of L. Viewing Ψ : G_K ↠ Γ as a continuous Λ^×-valued character and Λ^* = Hom_cts(Λ,Q_p/Z_p), set M = T ⊗_O Λ^*(Ψ^{-1}), the discrete Λ-module T ⊗_O Λ^* with G_K acting by ρ_{f,λ} ⊗ Ψ^{-1}. With S = {ℓ | pND}, Sel_∞(f,K,S) = ker{H^1(G_{K,S},M) → H^1(I_𝔭,M)}, its Pontryagin dual X_∞(f,K,S) = Hom_Λ(Sel_∞(f,K,S),Λ^*) is a finitely generated Λ-module, and Ch_Λ(f,K,S) is its characteristic ideal, non-zero exactly when X_∞(f,K,S) is Λ-torsion.
items.note: Review note on status: Partly planned. HeegnerPointEulerSystems:HE.8b plans the Greenberg Selmer group X_Gr over the anticyclotomic tower (strict at 𝔭, relaxed at 𝔭̄) and char(X_Gr)Λ^ur = (L_BDP²) for elliptic curves under the Heegner hypothesis. Consider citing HE.8b as the planned owner of the elliptic-curve case.

items.name: Characteristic ideals of finitely generated Iwasawa modules
items.statement: (i) Λ = O[[Γ]] ≅ O[[T]] and Λ^ur, and the two-variable O[[Γ_K]] and O^ur[[Γ_K]] (Γ_K ≅ Z_p²), are regular local rings, hence UFDs. The characteristic ideal of a finitely generated module over each is principal, and it is non-zero iff the module is torsion. (ii) Specialisation (the paper cites Skinner–Urban, Invent. Math. 195 (2014), Cor. 3.8): an inclusion of principal ideals char·A′ ⊆ (𝓛)·A′ over the two-variable ring (A′ = O^ur[[Γ_K]]⊗_O L) passes, along the map O^ur[[Γ_K]] → Λ^ur and the base change X ↦ X⊗Λ, to the corresponding inclusion over Λ^ur⊗_O L. (iii) For a finitely generated Λ-module X, Ch_Λ(X) ⊆ (γ−1) implies X/(γ−1)X is infinite.
items.locator: Used in §2.7, Skinner, Ann. of Math. (2) 191 (2020), 329–354
items.note: L4 plans the Weierstrass theory and the module structure over the Iwasawa algebra with characteristic ideals, L5 determinants, specialisation and exactness. Review (REV-PAPER-SKINNER-20): The statement covers only the one-variable algebra. The deduction of Proposition 2.7.2 also needs the two-variable rings and the passage of an inclusion of characteristic ideals through a specialisation, which the paper cites as Skinner–Urban Cor. 3.8. Review note on status: PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L4/L5 plan the one-variable theory. Check that the two-variable UFD and specialisation statements (ii) are also planned; if not, that part is missing.

items.name: Sel_∞ as a Greenberg Selmer group and the Panchishkin condition
items.statement: For ψ ∈ Σ^c_𝔭 of weight (−n,n) with n > 0, the induced representation Ind_{G_K}^{G_Q}(V ⊗ ψ^{-1}) satisfies Greenberg's Panchishkin condition: its restriction to G_{Q_p} is (V ⊗ ψ^{-1}) ⊕ (V ⊗ ψ^{-c}), the first summand being (V ⊗ ψ^{-1})|_{G_{K_𝔭}} with non-negative Hodge–Tate weights n and n−1 and the second (V ⊗ ψ^{-1})|_{G_{K_{𝔭̄}}} with negative weights −n and −n−1, and the subspace with negative weights has dimension equal to that of the +1-eigenspace of complex conjugation. Moreover M[γ−ψ(γ)] ≅ (T ⊗ ψ^{-1}) ⊗ Q_p/Z_p for a topological generator γ, so M is the discrete module of the deformation T ⊗ Λ(Ψ^{-1}) of T, which has a Zariski-dense set of Panchishkin specialisations, and Sel_∞(f,K,S) is the corresponding imprimitive Greenberg Selmer group. The conventions for Hodge–Tate weights are the negative of Greenberg's.
items.locator: §2.7, the paragraph following the definition of Ch_Λ, Skinner, Ann. of Math. (2) 191 (2020), 329–354 (Greenberg, Iwasawa theory and p-adic deformations of motives, §§3–4)
items.note: L0 plans the three formulations of the main conjecture, including the Greenberg/ordinary Selmer formulation with its Panchishkin subspace; L2 the Greenberg local conditions themselves. What is specific here is the G_K-version for the anticyclotomic deformation, recorded separately in PAPER-SKINNER-20/40. Review note on status: The note refers to 'PAPER-SKINNER-20/40', which is not an item id in this extraction. It presumably means PAPER-SKINNER-20/40.

items.name: The hypotheses (irr) and (irr_K)
items.statement: (irr): ρ̄_{f,λ} is an irreducible G_Q-representation. (irr_K): ρ̄_{f,λ}|_{G_K} is irreducible.

items.name: Conjecture 2.7.1: the Iwasawa–Greenberg main conjecture for M
items.statement: Conjecture 2.7.1. Assume p = 𝔭𝔭̄ splits in K, (sqf), (sgn), (ram), (flt), (odd), (L-lrg) (so that L^S_𝔭(f) ∈ O^ur[[Γ]] is defined) and (irr_K). Then Ch_Λ(f,K,S) and L^S_𝔭(f) generate the same ideal of Λ^ur ⊗_O L. This is essentially the Iwasawa–Greenberg main conjecture for M. The choice of L^S_𝔭(f) is dictated by the expectation that the order of the Selmer group of V ⊗ ψ^{-1} is related to L(V^∨ ⊗ ψ,1).
items.locator: Conjecture 2.7.1 with its footnote, Skinner, Ann. of Math. (2) 191 (2020), 329–354
items.note: Review (REV-PAPER-SKINNER-20): The statement omits the standing hypotheses under which L^S_𝔭(f) was introduced. Review note on status: The analogous equality for elliptic curves under the Heegner hypothesis (char(X_Gr)Λ^ur = (L_BDP²), BCS) is planned at HeegnerPointEulerSystems:HE.8b. Skinner's conjecture itself stays missing.

items.name: The hypotheses (big), (ord), (spl) and (res)
items.statement: (big): p ≥ 5. (ord): f is ordinary with respect to λ. (spl): both 2 and p split in K. (res): ρ̄_{f,λ} is ramified at some odd prime ℓ | N that is inert or ramified in K.
items.locator: §2.7, the displayed hypotheses before Proposition 2.7.2, Skinner, Ann. of Math. (2) 191 (2020), 329–354

items.name: Wan's Iwasawa main conjecture for Rankin–Selberg p-adic L-functions
items.statement: (Wan, Algebra Number Theory 14 (2020), Theorem 1.2 and its proof.) Let Γ_K ≅ Z_p² be the Galois group of the composite of all Z_p-extensions of K. Let f_0 be the ordinary stabilisation of f and ξ = ψ_0^alg ω as in item 47, so that π, f_0 and ξ satisfy the hypotheses of Wan's Theorem 1.2. Then, for Σ = S, the proof of that theorem shows that the ideal of O^ur[[Γ_K]] ⊗_O L generated by char_{O[[Γ_K]]}X^Σ_{f_0,K,ξ} is contained in the ideal generated by 𝓛^Σ_{f_0,K,ξ} ∈ O^ur[[Γ_K]] (Wan §7.5). Here Sel^Σ_{f_0,K,ξ} is Wan's Selmer group (§2.2), proved by the U(3,1) Eisenstein-congruence method following Skinner–Urban. The listed hypotheses (p ≥ 5, ordinarity, 2 and p split in K, residual irreducibility, ramification at an odd prime of N inert or ramified in K) are read off Remark 2.9.1.
items.locator: Used through Proposition 2.7.2, Skinner, Ann. of Math. (2) 191 (2020), 329–354 (Wan, Iwasawa main conjecture for Rankin–Selberg p-adic L-functions, Algebra Number Theory 14 (2020), 383–483, Theorem 1.2)
items.note: AutomorphicCongruences L2 plans the U(3,1) Eisenstein/Rankin–Selberg families and two-variable divisibility. This is the inclusion used in the proof of Wan’s Theorem 1.2, not a verbatim statement of that theorem. Published Skinner p.346 uses 𝓛^Σ_{f_0,K,ξ} and Wan §7.5 over O^ur[[Γ_K]]; arXiv v1 p.16 used 𝓛^{Σ,Hida}, an older theorem number and §6 over smaller coefficient rings. The published notation and unramified coefficient extension are used here.

items.name: Proposition 2.7.2 and its deduction from Wan's theorem
items.statement: Proposition 2.7.2. Under (sqf), (flt), (L-lrg), (irr_K), (sgn), (odd), (big), (ord), (spl) and (res), the ideal of Λ^ur ⊗_O L generated by Ch_Λ(f,K,S) is contained in the ideal generated by L^S_𝔭(f). The deduction: fix ψ_0 ∈ Σ^c_𝔭 of weight (−n_0,n_0) with n_0 > 6, let ψ^alg_0 be the associated algebraic Hecke character and ξ = ψ^alg_0 ω with ω the Teichmüller Hecke character; then π, the ordinary stabilisation f_0 of f, and ξ satisfy the hypotheses of Wan's theorem. Under the composition O^ur[[Γ_K]] → Λ^ur, γ ↦ ψ_0(γ)^{-1}γ, the function 𝓛^Σ_{f_0,K,ξ} maps to L^S_𝔭(f), and under the same base change Sel^Σ_{f_0,K,ξ} becomes Sel_∞(f,K,S) and X^Σ_{f_0,K,ξ} becomes X_∞(f,K,S); the inclusion of ideals then follows because the rings involved are unique factorisation domains and the characteristic ideals are principal.
items.locator: Proposition 2.7.2 with the two paragraphs explaining its deduction, Skinner, Ann. of Math. (2) 191 (2020), 329–354

items.name: The control diagram and the consequence of a vanishing p-adic L-value
items.statement: Let W = M[γ−1] = T ⊗ Q_p/Z_p, Sel_𝔭(f,K,S) = ker{H^1(G_{K,S},W) → H^1(I_𝔭,W)} and X_𝔭(f,K,S) its Pontryagin dual. Assuming (irr_K), H^1(G_{K,S},W) = H^1(G_{K,S},M)[γ−1], and the exactness of the bottom row of the commutative diagram built from 0 → W → M →^{γ−1} M → 0 shows that Sel_𝔭(f,K,S) is contained in Sel_∞(f,K,S)[γ−1] with finite index; hence (2.7.1) #X_𝔭(f,K,S) = ∞ ⟺ #(X_∞(f,K,S)/(γ−1)X_∞(f,K,S)) = ∞. If L^S_𝔭(f,1) = 0 then L^S_𝔭(f) ∈ (γ−1), so under Proposition 2.7.2 Ch_Λ(f,K,S) ⊆ (γ−1) and the coinvariants are infinite, giving (2.7.2) L^S_𝔭(f,1) = 0 ⟹ #X_𝔭(f,K,S) = ∞. Finally, since H^1(K_𝔭,V) ↪ H^1(I_𝔭,V), one has H^1_𝔭(K,V) = ker{H^1(G_{K,S},V) → H^1(I_𝔭,V)} and its image in H^1(G_{K,S},W) is the maximal divisible subgroup of Sel_𝔭(f,K,S).
items.locator: §2.7, the paragraphs containing (2.7.1) and (2.7.2), Skinner, Ann. of Math. (2) 191 (2020), 329–354

items.name: Proposition 2.7.3: a vanishing p-adic L-value forces a non-zero class in H^1_𝔭(K,V)
items.statement: Proposition 2.7.3. If the hypotheses of Proposition 2.7.2 hold, then L^S_𝔭(f,1) = 0 implies H^1_𝔭(K,V) ≠ 0.
items.locator: Proposition 2.7.3, Skinner, Ann. of Math. (2) 191 (2020), 329–354
items.note: H¹_𝔭(K,V) is the kernel of restriction at 𝔭: strict at 𝔭 and relaxed at 𝔭̄. The subscript names the strict prime (published p.339).

items.name: Lemma 2.8.1: (irr) and (res) imply (irr_K)
items.statement: Lemma 2.8.1. If (irr) and (res) hold, then so does (irr_K). (Proof: let ℓ | N be a prime at which ρ̄_{f,λ} is ramified; as ℓ || N the action of I_ℓ on V is unipotent and factors through tame inertia, so for a topological generator τ_ℓ of tame inertia at ℓ the element ρ_{f,λ}(τ_ℓ), hence ρ̄_{f,λ}(τ_ℓ), is unipotent of order a power of p; since τ_ℓ² ∈ G_K, the image of ρ̄_{f,λ}|_{G_K} contains a non-trivial unipotent element. If ρ̄_{f,λ}|_{G_K} were reducible over k̄ its image would lie in a torus, split or non-split, or in a Borel of GL_2(k); the torus is excluded by the unipotent element, so the image lies in a Borel, and since the image of G_K is normalised by the image of G_Q the image of G_Q lies in the same Borel, contradicting (irr).)
items.locator: Lemma 2.8.1 with its proof, Skinner, Ann. of Math. (2) 191 (2020), 329–354; the printed proof writes 'ρ̄_{f,λ} is reducible' where the hypothesis for contradiction must be on ρ̄_{f,λ}|_{G_K} (source issue E3)

items.name: The proof of Theorem B
items.statement: Under the hypotheses of Theorem B, (sqf), (odd) and (big) hold by assumption; (a) gives (flt) and (ord); (b) is (irr) and (res), so (irr_K) holds by Lemma 2.8.1; (c) is (spl); (e) gives (sgn) by Lemma 2.2.1. Propositions 2.7.2 and 2.7.3 then give: H^1_𝔭(K,V) = 0 implies L^S_𝔭(f,1) ≠ 0. Hypothesis (e) gives H^1_𝔭(K,V) = 0 by Lemma 2.3.2, and (d) is (ram), so Corollary 2.6.2 gives P_K(f) ≠ 0. The rank of A_f(K) is [M_f:Q] times the M_{f,p}-rank of A_f(K) ⊗ Q_p, at most dim_L H^1_f(K,V) = 1 by (e), and is non-zero since P_K(f) ≠ 0; hence rank_Z A_f(K) = [M_f:Q], and by Proposition 2.5.1 and Corollary 2.5.2, ord_{s=1}L(f,K,s) = 1 and ord_{s=1}L(A_f/K,s) = [M_f:Q]. Finiteness of Ш(A_f/K) reduces to that of Ш(A_f) and Ш(A_f^D); since L(f,K,s) = L(f,s)L(f ⊗ χ_D,s) has order 1 at s = 1, one factor has order 1 and the other order 0, and Gross–Zagier–Kolyvagin applies.

items.name: Remark 2.9.1: where each hypothesis is used
items.statement: Remark 2.9.1 records, in thirteen items, the provenance of each hypothesis: (i) squarefreeness comes from Wan and Brooks, and squarefreeness at the primes dividing (D,N) from Bertolini–Darmon–Prasanna; (ii) p ≥ 5 is imposed for convenience in Wan; (iii) D odd is imposed in Bertolini–Darmon–Prasanna, Brooks and Wan, and stems from gaps in the theta correspondence in residue characteristic 2; (iv) p ∤ N is used in the p-adic Gross–Zagier formulas and to simplify the appeal to the parity theorem; (v) ordinarity is used only for Wan's theorem and for the parity theorem, and a finite non-critical slope version of Proposition 2.7.2 together with the corresponding parity result would suffice; (vi) irreducibility and (res) are required in Wan, the latter to produce a transfer of π to a definite U(2) ramified at ℓ; (vii) the splitting of p in K is needed for all three p-adic inputs and for Lemma 2.3.2, and is the hardest to relax; (viii) the hypotheses in (d) are needed to appeal to Bertolini–Darmon–Prasanna, which requires ε_ℓ(f,K) = +1 for ℓ | (N,D); (ix) one-dimensionality of H^1_f(K,V) is used to know beforehand that ε(f,K) = −1; (x) the injectivity at p is needed for H^1_𝔭(K,V) = 0, and Wei Zhang obtains a version of Theorem B without it at the expense of Tamagawa hypotheses; (xi) the local hypotheses can likely be relaxed, for instance using Liu–Zhang–Zhang's general form of Proposition 2.6.1; (xii) the CM analogue is Rubin's Theorems 8.1, 8.2 and can also be proved along the present lines using the CM main conjecture and Rubin Theorem 9.5 or BDP Theorem 2; (xiii) the method can give an alternative proof of the base case of Wei Zhang's induction that avoids Skinner–Urban and should work at supersingular primes.
items.locator: Remark 2.9.1, Skinner, Ann. of Math. (2) 191 (2020), 329–354

items.name: Comparison with Wei Zhang's theorem on Kolyvagin's conjecture
items.statement: Wei Zhang proves many cases of a conjecture of Kolyvagin, showing that the p-adic Selmer group of A_f is often spanned by classes derived from Heegner points, and obtains a theorem similar to Theorem B. That theorem does not require the injectivity of the restriction map at the primes above p — the second half of hypothesis (e) — but crucially requires that the Tamagawa factors at the primes that split in K or are congruent to ±1 modulo p be indivisible by p, whereas Theorem B imposes no hypothesis on Tamagawa factors. There is substantial overlap but neither result subsumes the other; Zhang's proof also rests on Iwasawa theory, in his case on Skinner–Urban.
items.locator: §1, the paragraph before the acknowledgements, and Remark 2.9.1(x), Skinner, Ann. of Math. (2) 191 (2020), 329–354 (W. Zhang, Selmer groups and the indivisibility of Heegner points, Camb. J. Math. 2 (2014))

items.name: Density one of the ordinary primes for a non-CM newform
items.statement: For a newform f of weight two that is not a CM form, the set of primes p ∤ N such that f is ordinary with respect to some λ | p has density 1. (If f is not ordinary at any λ | p for a p ∤ N greater than 4 and unramified in M_f, then the norm of a_p(f), of absolute value at most (2p^{1/2})^{[M_f:Q]} by the Ramanujan bound, is an integer divisible by p^{[M_f:Q]}, so a_p(f) = 0; and the set of primes with a_p(f) = 0 has density zero.)
items.locator: §3, first paragraph, Skinner, Ann. of Math. (2) 191 (2020), 329–354 (Serre, Quelques applications du théorème de densité de Chebotarev, §7.2, Corollary 2)

items.name: Irreducibility of the residual representation for large p
items.statement: For a newform f without complex multiplication, ρ̄_{f,λ} is irreducible for all λ | p once p is sufficiently large.
items.locator: §3, second paragraph, Skinner, Ann. of Math. (2) 191 (2020), 329–354 (Ribet, On ℓ-adic representations attached to modular forms II, Glasgow Math. J. 27 (1985), Theorem 2.1)
items.note: Review note on status: For M_f = Q, residual irreducibility for all but finitely many p is planned at EllipticCurveModularity:R29.1. Ribet's result for general A_f is not planned.

items.name: Ramification of the residual representation at every prime dividing N
items.statement: Let f ∈ S_2(Γ_0(N)) be a newform with trivial character and N squarefree. For all sufficiently large p and every λ | p, ρ̄_{f,λ} is ramified at every prime ℓ | N. (Proof: take p ∤ N large enough that ρ̄_{f,λ} is irreducible. If for some ℓ | N there were arbitrarily large p with ρ̄_{f,λ} unramified at ℓ, level lowering would give newforms of weight 2 and level dividing N/ℓ congruent to f modulo primes of arbitrarily large residue characteristic. Only finitely many such newforms exist, so one of them, g, would have prime-to-Np coefficients equal to those of f, and f = g by strong multiplicity one, a contradiction.)
items.locator: §3, second paragraph, Skinner, Ann. of Math. (2) 191 (2020), 329–354 (Ribet, On modular representations of Gal(Q̄/Q) arising from modular forms, Invent. Math. 100 (1990))
items.note: Review (REV-PAPER-SKINNER-20): Hypotheses are missing. The argument uses N squarefree (ℓ || N), trivial character, the irreducibility of ρ̄_{f,λ} for p large (item 55), p ∤ N, and Ribet's level-lowering theorem. Review note on status: Its main input, Ribet's level-lowering theorem, is planned at SerreWeightAndLevelOptimisation:R20.2. The argument itself is missing.

items.name: The choice of the auxiliary imaginary quadratic field
items.statement: Under the hypotheses of Theorem A one chooses an imaginary quadratic K of discriminant D with: (i) 2 and p split in K, so D is odd and hypothesis (c) of Theorem B holds; (ii) if for some odd ℓ the representation π_ℓ is the twist of the special representation by the unramified quadratic character, then K is ramified at ℓ and all other prime divisors of N split in K; (iii) if there is no such π_ℓ but there are two odd primes ℓ_1, ℓ_2 with π_{ℓ_1}, π_{ℓ_2} special, then ℓ_1 and ℓ_2 are inert in K and all other prime divisors of N split in K; (iv) L(f ⊗ χ_D,1) ≠ 0. Conditions (i)–(ii) give ε(f,K) = −ε_ℓ(π,K) = −1 and (i)–(iii) give ε(f,K) = −ε_{ℓ_1}(π,K)ε_{ℓ_2}(π,K) = −1, so ε(f ⊗ χ_D) = −ε(f) = +1 and (iv) can then also be arranged; (i)–(iii) imply hypotheses (b), (c), (d) of Theorem B.
items.locator: §3, the list (i)–(iv) and the paragraph following it, Skinner, Ann. of Math. (2) 191 (2020), 329–354

items.name: Non-vanishing of quadratic twists in the sign +1 branch
items.statement: Given a newform f and finitely many local conditions on the discriminant compatible with a sign ε(f ⊗ χ_D) = +1, there is an imaginary quadratic field K of discriminant D satisfying those conditions with L(f ⊗ χ_D,1) ≠ 0. This is Theorem B of Friedberg–Hoffstein.
items.locator: Used in §3, condition (iv), Skinner, Ann. of Math. (2) 191 (2020), 329–354 (Friedberg–Hoffstein, Ann. of Math. (2) 142 (1995), 385–423, Theorem B)
items.note: BSD.2 plans exactly the quadratic-twist non-vanishing theorem with finitely many prescribed splitting and local conditions compatible with the functional equation, naming the BFH/Friedberg–Hoffstein unfolding as its proof route.

items.name: The proof of Theorem A
items.statement: Assume all hypotheses of Theorem A (item 5). Squarefree level implies f is non-CM (item 65). The density-one ordinary-prime result (54), residual irreducibility (55) and ramification for all sufficiently large p at every ℓ|N (56) give p≥5, p∤N, and λ|p such that f is λ-ordinary and the residual representation is irreducible and ramified at every ℓ|N. The rational Kummer comparison gives dim_L H¹_f(Q,V)=1 (78), and parity (18) gives ε(f)=−1. Choose an imaginary quadratic K of discriminant D with 2 and p split; if an odd ℓ has the unramified-quadratic-twist local component, make ℓ ramified and all other primes of N split; otherwise make the two selected special odd primes inert and all remaining primes of N split (57). The twist has sign +1, and Friedberg–Hoffstein (58) allows L(f⊗χ_D,1)≠0 with these local conditions. The rank-zero forward theorem (2, alternatively 60), and quadratic restriction/trace and Sha comparisons (66), give rank_Z A_f(K)=[M_f:Q] and finite Ш(A_f/K)[p^∞]. Lemma 2.2.2 as repaired by 81–82 (item 20) gives B(e). The chosen p, λ and K give B(a)–(d) with exactly the hypotheses in item 7. Theorem B gives ord_{s=1}L(f,K,s)=1; the factorization L(f,K,s)=L(f,s)L(f⊗χ_D,s) and the nonzero second central value imply ord_{s=1}L(f,s)=1.
items.note: Complete published §3 deduction, with the omitted eigencomponent-logarithm proof now imported from Burungale–Skinner–Wan. No additional choice of a unique prime λ above p is needed.

items.name: Kato's Euler system as an alternative to Gross–Zagier–Kolyvagin at rank zero
items.statement: The finiteness of A_f^D(Q) and Ш(A_f^D) from L(f ⊗ χ_D,1) ≠ 0 can be deduced from Kato's Euler system instead of from the work of Gross, Zagier and Kolyvagin.
items.locator: §3, the paragraph deducing hypothesis (e), Skinner, Ann. of Math. (2) 191 (2020), 329–354 (Kato, Astérisque 295 (2004), 117–290)
items.note: KatoEulerSystems L4 plans the non-vanishing and cohomological theorems of Kato's system and BSD.4 records the Kato route to the analytic-rank-zero statement as an explicitly scoped alternative.

items.name: The deduction of Theorem C from Theorem B
items.statement: Under the hypotheses of Theorem C: (a) and (b) give Sel_{p^∞}(E) ≅ Q_p/Z_p by the Cassels–Tate pairing, so dim H^1_f(Q,V) = 1; (c) makes H^1_f(Q,V) → H^1_f(Q_p,V) ≅ Q_p an isomorphism. By Ribet's level lowering, E[p] is ramified at some odd prime ℓ of bad reduction. Choose K inert or ramified at ℓ according as E has split or non-split reduction at ℓ, with the remaining conditions of Theorem B (2 and p split; sign −1; L(E^D,1) ≠ 0 by Friedberg–Hoffstein). Theorem B then applies as in §3.
items.locator: §3, final paragraph, Skinner, Ann. of Math. (2) 191 (2020), 329–354
items.note: Review (REV-PAPER-SKINNER-20): The sketch attributes H^1_f(Q,V) ≅ H^1_f(Q_p,V) to hypothesis (c) alone. It also needs (a) and (b) together with the Cassels–Tate pairing: (a) and (b) give Sel_{p^∞}(E) ≅ Q_p/Z_p. It also needs E(Q_p)[p^∞] = E(Q_p)[p] for p ≥ 5 of good reduction. See the new coverage item. The missing Cassels–Tate prerequisites are now separate shared items 83–86, imported by 74; no global Sha finiteness is assumed at this stage.

items.name: The proof of Theorem E
items.statement: The argument is that of Theorem A with two changes. First, the hypotheses give dim_L H^1_f(Q,V) = 0, so ε(f) = +1 by Nekovář. Second, K is chosen to satisfy (i), (ii), (iii) and (iv)′ ord_{s=1}L(f⊗χ_D,s) = 1. This is possible because ε(f⊗χ_D) = −1 and a derivative non-vanishing theorem for quadratic twists with prescribed local behaviour applies (Bump–Friedberg–Hoffstein, Invent. Math. 102 (1990); Murty–Murty, Ann. of Math. 133 (1991)). Theorem B then gives ord_{s=1}L(f,K,s) = 1, whence L(f,1) ≠ 0.
items.note: Theorem E uses item 76 for the sign −1 derivative-nonvanishing choice of K; E11 retains the omitted citation. The forward rank-one theorem for the twist gives rank_Z A_f(K)=[M_f:Q] and finite p-primary Ш; items 81–82 and 20 supply B(e). E5 is a repaired historical omission, not an extra hypothesis of E.

items.name: Local components at primes ℓ || N and Atkin–Lehner eigenvalues
items.statement: Let f ∈ S_2(Γ_0(N)) be a newform with trivial character and π = ⊗π_v the cuspidal automorphic representation of GL_2(A) with L(π,s−1/2) = L(f,s). If ℓ || N, then π_ℓ is either the special (Steinberg) representation σ_ℓ or its twist σ_ℓ⊗ξ_ℓ by the unramified quadratic character ξ_ℓ of Q_ℓ^×. Moreover a_ℓ(f) = ±1 and the Atkin–Lehner involution w_ℓ acts on f by −a_ℓ(f): π_ℓ ≅ σ_ℓ ⟺ a_ℓ(f) = 1 ⟺ w_ℓ f = −f, and π_ℓ ≅ σ_ℓ⊗ξ_ℓ ⟺ a_ℓ(f) = −1 ⟺ w_ℓ f = f. For f attached to an elliptic curve E, π_ℓ ≅ σ_ℓ exactly when E has split multiplicative reduction at ℓ, and π_ℓ ≅ σ_ℓ⊗ξ_ℓ exactly when it is non-split.
items.locator: §1, the paragraph after Theorem A and the passage to Theorem A′ (pp. 330–331); §2.5, the paragraph after (sqf), (sgn) (p. 341)
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-SKINNER-20 (coverage of the published text): Theorems A, A′ and E, the (ram) hypothesis and the sign computations all use the fact that π_ℓ is σ_ℓ or σ_ℓ⊗ξ_ℓ and how this matches w_ℓ and the reduction type. No item states it. Check that the relation w_ℓ = −a_ℓ(f) for ℓ || N is in ModularForms layer 6; if it is not, that relation is missing.

items.name: Theorem A′ from Theorem A
items.statement: Let E/Q be a semistable elliptic curve of conductor N. Then N is squarefree, and by the modularity theorem there is a newform f ∈ S_2(Γ_0(N)) with trivial character and M_f = Q such that A_f is Q-isogenous to E and L(E,s) = L(f,s). By the local-component dictionary, E has non-split (resp. split) multiplicative reduction at ℓ exactly when π_ℓ ≅ σ_ℓ⊗ξ_ℓ (resp. σ_ℓ). Rank and finiteness of Ш are isogeny invariants. Hence Theorem A for f is Theorem A′ for E.
items.locator: §1, the sentence before Theorem A′, p. 330
items.note: The assembly uses modularity and the quotient/L-function comparison from R29.5–R29.6, the local-component dictionary from item 63, the explicit isogeny comparison in item 91, and Skinner’s Theorem A (5). It belongs to the existing RankOneConverse route; modularity alone does not supply the converse.

items.name: No complex multiplication at squarefree level
items.statement: Let f ∈ S_2(Γ_0(N)) be a newform with trivial character and N squarefree. Then f is not a CM form, and A_f does not have complex multiplication. (A weight-two CM newform of trivial character, with CM by K, has level |d_K|·N(𝔣) where the conductor 𝔣 of its Hecke character is divisible by the primes ramified in K, so ℓ² | N for every ℓ | d_K.)
items.locator: §1, p. 330; §3, first sentence, p. 350
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-SKINNER-20 (coverage of the published text): Used to invoke Serre's density result (item 54) and to separate the paper's cases from Rubin's CM case (item 4).  Route: the Part II.

items.name: Rank and Ш under quadratic base change
items.statement: Let K be imaginary quadratic with character χ_D and p an odd prime. Then rank_Z A_f(K) = rank_Z A_f(Q) + rank_Z A_f^D(Q). Ш(A_f/K)[p^∞] is finite iff Ш(A_f)[p^∞] and Ш(A_f^D)[p^∞] are finite, and Ш(A_f/K) is finite iff Ш(A_f) and Ш(A_f^D) are finite. Also L(A_f/K,s) = L(A_f,s)L(A_f^D,s). (Use Shapiro's lemma for Res_{K/Q}A_f and the Q-isogeny A_f × A_f^D → Res_{K/Q}A_f, whose kernel and cokernel are killed by 2.)
items.locator: §1, the deduction of Theorem A, p. 332; §2.9, p. 348; §3, p. 351
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-SKINNER-20 (coverage of the published text): Used in the deductions of Theorems A and E and in the proof of Theorem B. Item 13 records only the isogeny. RankZeroOneBSD:BSD.0–BSD.1 plan the elliptic-curve case (factorisation of L(E/K,s) and descent of Sha finiteness). Route: the Part II.

items.name: Néron–Tate pairing and its non-degeneracy on the f-isotypic part
items.statement: Let 𝓛 be a symmetric ample line bundle on A_f/Q with polarisation λ_𝓛. Then ⟨P,Q⟩_𝓛 = ⟨P,λ_𝓛(Q)⟩_{NT} is a positive definite quadratic form on A_f(K)⊗R. Since the Rosati involution fixes the totally real field M_f, ⟨aP,Q⟩_𝓛 = ⟨P,aQ⟩_𝓛 for a ∈ M_f. Extend ⟨,⟩_𝓛 M_f-linearly to A_f(K)⊗M_f and evaluate through ι: M_f ⊂ R. Then ⟨x,x⟩_𝓛 ≠ 0 for every non-zero x in the ε_f-isotypic part, so P_K(f) ≠ 0 iff ⟨P_K(f),P_K(f)⟩_𝓛 ≠ 0.
items.locator: §2.5, the proof of Proposition 2.5.1, p. 341
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-SKINNER-20 (coverage of the published text): The Néron–Tate height pairing and its non-degeneracy on the f-isotypic part are key inputs of Proposition 2.5.1 and are not an item. The isotypic non-degeneracy is an addition to RP.0's canonical heights.

items.name: Case II global Jacquet–Langlands transfer
items.statement: In Case II, N=N⁻N⁺ with N⁻ a nontrivial product of an even number of primes inert in K and N⁺ supported on split primes. Let B/Q be the quaternion algebra of discriminant N⁻, split at the real place, and take an Eichler order of level N⁺. The global Jacquet–Langlands transfer of the weight-two newform f yields a weight-two quaternionic cuspform f_B with the same Hecke eigenvalues a_ℓ(f) for ℓ∤N, unique up to nonzero scalar.
items.locator: §2.4, Case II, p. 340; §1, p. 333 ('A_f is a quotient of the Jacobian of some Shimura curve')
items.note: R17.3 supplies global transfer and uniqueness with its local and parity hypotheses. The curve and cohomology are separate items 87–88, the quotient/differential realization is 89, and the precise Skinner/Brooks normalization comparison is missing item 90. R18.3’s definite finite class set is not the direct curve supplier.

items.name: The complex and p-adic CM periods Ω and Ω_p
items.statement: Fix an elliptic curve E_0 with CM by O_K, defined over a number field with good reduction at the prime above 𝔭 fixed by the embedding, and a Néron differential ω_0. The complex period Ω ∈ C^× is the period of ω_0. The p-adic period Ω_p ∈ (O^ur)^× is defined by ω_0 = Ω_p·ω_can, where ω_can is the differential attached to a trivialisation of the formal group of E_0 over O^ur (Katz). Both are normalised as in Bertolini–Darmon–Prasanna [2] §5, the paper's reference for the formula.
items.locator: §2.6, the bullets after the interpolation formula, p. 343
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-SKINNER-20 (coverage of the published text): The complex and p-adic CM periods enter the interpolation formula (item 34). The p-adic period is why L^S_𝔭(f) lies in O^ur[[Γ]] (E1). The paper does not define them. Ω_p is a unit of O^ur and in general does not lie in L. This is the source of E1.

items.name: Serre: supersingular-type primes have density zero
items.statement: If f ∈ S_2(Γ_0(N)) is a newform without complex multiplication, then the set of primes p with a_p(f) = 0 has natural density zero (Serre, Publ. Math. IHÉS 54 (1981), §7.2, Cor. 2).
items.locator: §3, first paragraph, p. 350
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-SKINNER-20 (coverage of the published text): Item 54 is the consequence. Its two key inputs, Serre's density theorem and the Ramanujan bound, are not items.  Route: the AutomorphicGaloisRepresentations source route.

items.name: Ramanujan bound in weight two
items.statement: For a newform f ∈ S_2(Γ_0(N)), a prime p ∤ N and every embedding σ: M_f ↪ C, |σ(a_p(f))| ≤ 2√p. Hence |N_{M_f/Q}(a_p(f))| ≤ (2√p)^{[M_f:Q]}.
items.locator: §3, first paragraph, p. 350
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-SKINNER-20 (coverage of the published text): A key input of item 54. Via the Eichler–Shimura relation (R19.1) and the Weil bound for curves (WC.5).

items.name: Ribet's level-lowering theorem
items.statement: Let p be an odd prime and f ∈ S_2(Γ_0(N)) a newform with trivial character, with p ∤ N. Let λ | p be a prime with ρ̄_{f,λ} irreducible. Let ℓ || N, ℓ ≠ p, be a prime at which ρ̄_{f,λ} is unramified. Then there is a newform g of weight 2, trivial character and level dividing N/ℓ such that ρ̄_{g,λ′} ≅ ρ̄_{f,λ} for a prime λ′ above p (in a common coefficient field). In particular a_q(g) ≡ a_q(f) mod λ′ for all primes q ∤ Np. (Ribet, Invent. Math. 100 (1990), Theorem 1.1.)
items.locator: §3, second paragraph and final paragraph, pp. 350–351; §1, p. 332
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-SKINNER-20 (coverage of the published text): Used in item 56 and in the deduction of Theorem C (item 61). Neither item states the theorem.

items.name: Strong multiplicity one for weight-two newforms
items.statement: If two newforms f, g of weight 2 and trivial character have a_q(f) = a_q(g) for all but finitely many primes q, then f = g. In particular they have the same level.
items.locator: §3, second paragraph, p. 350
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-SKINNER-20 (coverage of the published text): A key input of item 56.

items.name: Selmer hypotheses of Theorem C give hypothesis (e) over Q
items.statement: Let E/Q be an elliptic curve, p ≥ 5 a prime of good ordinary reduction with E[p] irreducible and Sel_p(E) ≅ Z/pZ. Then Sel_{p^∞}(E) ≅ Q_p/Z_p. (E(Q)[p] = 0 gives Sel_{p^∞}(E)[p] ≅ Sel_p(E). A finite non-zero cyclic Sel_{p^∞}(E) would equal Ш(E)[p^∞], contradicting the Cassels–Tate structure Ш(E)[p^∞] ≅ X ⊕ X.) Hence dim_{Q_p}H^1_f(Q,V_pE) = 1. If moreover the image of Sel_p(E) → E(Q_p)/pE(Q_p) is not contained in the image of E(Q_p)[p], then H^1_f(Q,V_pE) → H^1_f(Q_p,V_pE) ≅ Q_p is an isomorphism. This uses E(Q_p)[p^∞] = E(Q_p)[p] for p ≥ 5 of good reduction.
items.locator: §3, final paragraph, p. 351
items.note: The Selmer corank argument imports the shared pairing and structure results 83–86 from SelmerIwasawaCohomology L1–L2. If the cofinite-type p-primary Selmer group with p-torsion F_p were finite, it would be nonzero cyclic; the Kummer sequence would then identify it with finite Ш[p^∞], contradicting the paired elementary divisors in 86. Only that conditional p-primary finiteness is used. The remaining local non-torsion-image step and the good-reduction p-power torsion bound are as in the inherited statement. RankOneConverse owns this assembly, not the Cassels–Tate pairing.

items.name: E[p] is ramified at an odd bad prime
items.statement: Let E/Q be semistable and p ≥ 5 a prime of good reduction with E[p] irreducible. Then E[p] is ramified at some odd prime ℓ at which E has (multiplicative) bad reduction. (Otherwise repeated level lowering at every odd ℓ | N, with E[p] finite flat at p, would realise E[p] in S_2(Γ_0(M)) for some M | 2. That space is zero.)
items.locator: §3, final paragraph, p. 351
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-SKINNER-20 (coverage of the published text): A step of the deduction of Theorem C that is not an item. Its input, Ribet's level lowering, is planned at SerreWeightAndLevelOptimisation:R20.2. Route: the Part II.

items.name: Non-vanishing of first derivatives of quadratic twists
items.statement: Let f ∈ S_2(Γ_0(N)) be a newform. Fix finitely many primes, a prescribed splitting behaviour of K at each (split, inert or ramified), and D < 0, compatible with ε(f⊗χ_D) = −1. Then there are infinitely many imaginary quadratic fields K of discriminant D with that behaviour and L′(f⊗χ_D,1) ≠ 0, so that ord_{s=1}L(f⊗χ_D,s) = 1. (Bump–Friedberg–Hoffstein, Invent. Math. 102 (1990); Murty–Murty, Ann. of Math. 133 (1991).)
items.locator: §4, condition (iv)′, p. 352 (no citation in the paper)
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-SKINNER-20 (coverage of the published text): The proof of Theorem E needs this theorem. Item 58 covers only central values in the sign +1 branch. BSD.2 plans 'twists with a nonzero first derivative in the sign − branch'. See new source issue new-7.

items.name: The formal logarithm log_ω
items.statement: Let ω ∈ Ω^1(A_f)⊗M_f with φ^*ω = ω_f, so that M_f acts on ω through Ω^1(A_f) by its scalar action. log_ω : A_f(K_𝔭) ⊗ L → K̄_𝔭 is the L-linear extension of the p-adic logarithm of A_f over K_𝔭 = Q_p attached to ω: the homomorphism A_f(K_𝔭) → K̄_𝔭 given near 0 by integrating ω along the formal group, extended to all of A_f(K_𝔭) using finiteness of the component and torsion quotients. It is M_f-linear via the embedding M_f ↪ L fixed by λ. It vanishes on the λ-component of a point P iff the λ-component of the Kummer image of P in H^1_f(K_𝔭,V) vanishes (Bloch–Kato logarithm).
items.locator: §1, p. 333; §2.6, after Proposition 2.6.1, p. 344
items.note: GZ.9 plans the formal/Bloch–Kato logarithm and exact differential/Kummer comparison. Algebraic-point eigencomponent nonvanishing is a separate missing input, items 81–82. It does not follow merely from a cohomology class being nonzero; GZ.9’s warning remains valid.

items.name: Selmer dimension over Q
items.statement: If Ш(A_f)[p^∞] is finite then dim_L H^1_f(Q,V) = rank_Z A_f(Q)/[M_f:Q]. In particular dim_L H^1_f(Q,V) = 1 if rank_Z A_f(Q) = [M_f:Q], and 0 if A_f(Q) is finite. (A_f(Q)⊗Q_p ≅ H^1_f(Q,V_pA_f) is free over M_{f,p}, and H^1_f(Q,V) = H^1_f(Q,V_pA_f) ⊗_{M_{f,p}} L.)
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-SKINNER-20 (coverage of the published text): The Q-version is used twice and is not an item.  Route: the Part II.

items.name: p-adic analytic subgroup theorem for an algebraic point on an abelian variety
items.statement: Fix an embedding Q̄→C_p. Let A/Q̄ be an abelian variety, x∈A(Q̄) non-torsion, and W⊆Lie(A) a Q̄-linear subspace. If log_A(x)∈W⊗_{Q̄}C_p, there are an abelian subvariety B⊆A and a nonzero integer m with Lie(B)⊆W and [m]x∈B(Q̄).
items.locator: Burungale–Skinner–Wan, arXiv:2603.20886v2 (10 May 2026), Theorem 3.1 and the identity-component formulation, pp.9–10
items.note: The non-torsion specialization needed here; the source first gives an algebraic subgroup containing x and then passes to its identity component. Proposed additional source at DT.3, not a claim that its current logarithmic-form contract already contains this theorem.

items.name: Endomorphism-stable p-adic analytic subgroup theorem
items.statement: In item 79 suppose a number field F embeds in End⁰_{Q̄}(A) and W is F-stable. Then B can be chosen F-stable, with a compatible embedding F→End⁰_{Q̄}(B), Lie(B)⊆W and [m]x∈B(Q̄) for some nonzero integer m.
items.locator: Burungale–Skinner–Wan, arXiv:2603.20886v2 (10 May 2026), Theorem 3.2, p.10
items.note: Non-torsion specialization. The proof sums the images of the analytic subgroup under an integral basis of an endomorphism order and takes the identity component. The general transcendence input has one proposed owner at DT.3.

items.name: Algebraic-point nonvanishing in every real-multiplication eigencomponent
items.statement: Fix an embedding Q̄→C_p. Let A/Q̄ be an abelian variety with a number field F⊆End⁰_{Q̄}(A), dim A=[F:Q], and at least one real embedding of F. For every non-torsion x∈A(Q̄), every σ:F→Q̄, and every nonzero F-eigendifferential ω∈H⁰(A,Ω¹) with a*ω=σ(a)ω for all a∈F, one has log_ω(x)≠0.
items.locator: Burungale–Skinner–Wan, arXiv:2603.20886v2 (10 May 2026), Theorem 1.1, p.3; Theorem 2.3/Remark 2.4, p.5; §4.1, p.10
items.note: The field need only have a real embedding; M_f is totally real and so qualifies. A rank-one theorem independent of the structural-rank Conjecture 5.2. Proposed DT.3 source extension, importing existing abelian-variety and tangent carriers; no proof duplication in RankOneConverse.

items.name: RM rational points and the ε_f Heegner projection have nonzero eigenlogarithms
items.statement: For the modular A_f with totally real M_f and dim A_f=[M_f:Q], every actual non-torsion algebraic point has nonzero logarithm for each nonzero M_f-eigendifferential. In Skinner’s Cases I/II, let Q^ξ_K∈J(X)(K)⊗Q be the rational Hodge-divisor class, y=φ(Q^ξ_K)∈A_f(K)⊗Q, and P_K(f)=φ(ε_f Q^ξ_K). For the differential ω with φ*ω=ω_f (or the normalized f_B differential), functoriality and ε_f*ω_f=ω_f give log_ω P_K(f)=log_ω y. If P_K(f)≠0, then y≠0; choose a positive integer m with [m]y an actual point of A_f(K). It is non-torsion, so item 81 gives log_ω([m]y)≠0 and hence log_ω P_K(f)≠0. In Case I one may instead use Q⁰_K and its cusp comparison.
items.locator: Skinner §§2.4–2.6, pp.340–344; Burungale–Skinner–Wan, arXiv:2603.20886v2 (10 May 2026), §§1.2–1.4 and Theorem 1.1
items.note: Proposed missing application at GZ.9 of the DT.3 theorem. It explicitly passes through a rational divisor point before applying algebraic-point transcendence; it asserts nothing about an arbitrary nonzero M_f- or C_p-linear tensor, or arbitrary nonzero cohomology class. It uses the existing Heegner construction from HE.1 and the normalization comparison, not another construction.
