items.name: The elliptic Cassels–Tate pairing
items.statement: For an elliptic curve E over a number field F, let Ш(E/F) be the kernel of H¹(F,E)→∏_v H¹(F_v,E). The Cassels–Tate pairing, using the canonical principal polarization E≅E∨, is a canonical bilinear map ⟨ , ⟩_CT:Ш(E/F)×Ш(E/F)→Q/Z.
items.locator: Poonen–Stoll, The Cassels–Tate pairing on polarized abelian varieties, corrected author version (23 August 2014), §1, p.2; general construction in §3
items.note: Cassels’ original elliptic construction and Tate’s generalization, recalled and developed in this public source. Proposed shared source at SelmerIwasawaCohomology L1–L2. Import the actual local/global duality from ArithmeticGaloisDuality and the existing Sha carrier; do not reconstruct them. No finiteness assumption on Ш.

items.name: Cassels–Tate kernels and nondegeneracy modulo divisibility
items.statement: For E/F as in item 83, the left and right kernels of ⟨ , ⟩_CT are the maximal divisible subgroup Ш(E/F)_div. Thus it induces a nondegenerate pairing on Ш(E/F)/Ш(E/F)_div in both variables.
items.locator: Poonen–Stoll, The Cassels–Tate pairing on polarized abelian varieties, corrected author version (23 August 2014), §1, p.2
items.note: Nondegeneracy modulo divisibility is unconditional; perfectness of a finite p-primary group is used only after that group’s finiteness is established.

items.name: Alternation of the elliptic Cassels–Tate pairing
items.statement: For E/F as in item 83 and every x∈Ш(E/F), ⟨x,x⟩_CT=0.
items.locator: Poonen–Stoll, The Cassels–Tate pairing on polarized abelian varieties, corrected author version (23 August 2014), §1, p.2
items.note: This is the elliptic theorem of Cassels. It is not unconditional alternation for an arbitrary principally polarized abelian variety; Poonen–Stoll explicitly distinguish those cases.

items.name: Finite odd-primary Sha has paired elementary divisors
items.statement: For an elliptic curve E over a number field F and an odd prime p, assume only that Ш(E/F)[p^∞] is finite. Its restricted Cassels–Tate pairing is perfect and alternating; consequently Ш(E/F)[p^∞]≅H⊕H for some finite abelian p-group H. In particular its order is a square, its p-torsion has even F_p-dimension, and it cannot be a nonzero cyclic p-group.
items.locator: Poonen–Stoll, The Cassels–Tate pairing on polarized abelian varieties, corrected author version (23 August 2014), §1, p.2 and the finite alternating-pairing consequence used in Skinner §3, p.351
items.note: Cross-primary pairings vanish and the p-primary part of the divisible kernel is zero under this finiteness assumption. Paired elementary divisors, not square cardinality alone, exclude a cyclic group (a cyclic group of order p² also has square cardinality). Global finiteness of Ш is not assumed.

items.name: The Case II indefinite Shimura curve
items.statement: In Skinner Case II, N=N⁻N⁺ as in item 68, B/Q is indefinite of discriminant N⁻, and an Eichler order has level N⁺. The associated quaternionic Shimura datum has a canonical curve X/Q with the specified level and complex uniformization, with level/stabilizer conventions retained.
items.locator: Skinner §2.4, p.340; Brooks §§2.1–2.2
items.note: Indefinite curve owner. The definite class set of R18.3 is not this object.

items.name: Hecke-compatible cohomological realization on the Case II curve
items.statement: In Skinner Case II, N=N⁻N⁺ as in item 68, B/Q is indefinite of discriminant N⁻, and an Eichler order has level N⁺. The Hecke action on the Betti and étale cohomology of the curve X is compatible with comparison and with the weight-two Jacquet–Langlands realization; its f-isotypic part is the realization having the Hecke eigenvalues of f away from N.
items.locator: Skinner §2.4, pp.339–340 (realization input); R18.4 contract
items.note: Import the existing cohomology/Hecke comparison; normalization as a particular differential remains item 90.

items.name: The Case II modular abelian quotient and differential pullback
items.statement: In Skinner Case II, N=N⁻N⁺ as in item 68, B/Q is indefinite of discriminant N⁻, and an Eichler order has level N⁺. Up to Q-isogeny the abelian variety A_f is the f-quotient of J(X), with a rational modular quotient φ and its compatible Hecke action. Pullback identifies the chosen eigendifferential on A_f with the weight-two f_B eigenline on X; the scalar depends on the choice of normalization.
items.locator: Skinner §2.4, p.340 and §2.5, p.341
items.note: GZ.3 already plans rational automorphic realizations, field of definition, quotient parametrizations and exact differential comparison on the existing curve. It does not fix the particular scalar of Skinner’s use of Brooks.

items.name: Skinner–Brooks rational normalization adapter in Case II
items.statement: In Skinner Case II, N=N⁻N⁺ as in item 68, B/Q is indefinite of discriminant N⁻, and an Eichler order has level N⁺. Choose the f_B eigenform over M_f using the rational realization of item 89, with the scalar convention compatible with Brooks’ transfer normalization. Choose ω on A_f with φ*ω=ω_{f_B}. The ε_f projection of the rational Hodge-divisor class then defines Skinner’s Q_K(f_B) and P_K(f_B), and their logarithmic comparison with Brooks Proposition 8.13 uses that same differential and the nonzero normalization scalar (including C(f,K)=α(f,f_GL2)^{-1}).
items.locator: Skinner §2.4, p.340 (cites Brooks §2.8), §§2.6, pp.343–344; published Brooks §2.7, p.4190 and §2.8, pp.4190–4191; see E12
items.note: Missing Skinner-specific adapter in RankOneConverse. Preserve the original §2.8 citation as provenance but use the published §2.7 transfer normalization. A generic rational transfer theorem or the definite class set does not by itself identify this scalar. Reuse HE.1’s CM/Hodge-point construction; do not assume a canonical normalization or scalar one.

items.name: Elliptic rank and Sha-finiteness comparison under isogeny
items.statement: Let E and E′ be elliptic curves over a number field F and φ:E→E′ an F-isogeny. Then φ induces E(F)⊗Q≅E′(F)⊗Q, so their Mordell–Weil ranks agree, and Ш(E/F) is finite if and only if Ш(E′/F) is finite.
items.locator: Implicit in Skinner §1, pp.330–331, deduction of A′; EllipticCurves Layer 7 and RankZeroOneBSD BSD.1
items.note: Reuse the existing isogeny-Selmer/dual-isogeny comparisons and transfer of Sha finiteness explicitly required by EllipticCurves Layer 7; BSD.1 imports them alongside its quadratic-descent comparisons. This is a planned input, not a consequence of modularity and not a library theorem.

prerequisites.citation: Xin Wan, "Iwasawa main conjecture for Rankin–Selberg p-adic L-functions", Algebra & Number Theory 14 (2020), no. 2, 383–483
prerequisites.why: Theorem 1.2 is the only source of the divisibility Ch_Λ(f,K,S) ⊆ (L^S_𝔭(f)) that makes Proposition 2.7.2 and hence the whole argument work. Its proof is the U(3,1) Eisenstein-congruence method of Skinner–Urban, with the two-variable p-adic L-function 𝓛^Σ_{f_0,K,ξ} over Γ_K ≅ Z_p²; its hypotheses are exactly (big), (ord), (spl), (res), (irr_K) and the squarefreeness of N. Nothing in this paper reproves it. The 2013 Columbia preprint cited in the arXiv version and the published paper are not interchangeable. Published notation is from Skinner p.346/Wan §7.5 over O^ur[[Γ_K]]; the preprint’s Σ,Hida, §6 and older theorem number are a separate version, as item 46 explains.

prerequisites.citation: Massimo Bertolini, Henri Darmon and Kartik Prasanna, "p-adic Rankin L-series and rational points on CM elliptic curves", Pacific J. Math. 260 (2012), no. 2, 261–303, and "Generalized Heegner cycles and p-adic Rankin L-series", Duke Math. J. 162 (2013), no. 6, 1033–1148
prerequisites.why: Theorem 3.12 of the first is Proposition 2.6.1 in Case I, and the second constructs the anticyclotomic p-adic L-function L_p(f,χ) on Σ^{(2)}_{cc}(𝔫) with the interpolation formula whose imprimitive variant is L^S_𝔭(f). Their hypotheses — N squarefree at the primes dividing (D,N), D odd, p ∤ N split in K, ε_ℓ(f,K) = +1 for ℓ | (N,D) — are carried into Theorem B as (d), (odd) and (flt).

prerequisites.citation: Ernest Hunter Brooks, "Shimura curves and special values of p-adic L-functions", Int. Math. Res. Not. IMRN 2015, no. 12, 4177–4241
prerequisites.why: Proposition 8.13 is Proposition 2.6.1 in Case II, on the Shimura curve of discriminant N^- with an Eichler order of level N^+, together with the normalisation of the Jacquet–Langlands transfer f_B over M_f (Skinner cites §2.8; the published Brooks transfer normalization is §2.7, p.4190; see E12) and the constant α(f,f_{GL_2})^{-1} that is C(f,K) here.

prerequisites.citation: Xinyi Yuan, Shou-Wu Zhang and Wei Zhang, "The Gross–Zagier Formula on Shimura Curves", Annals of Mathematics Studies 184, Princeton University Press, 2013
prerequisites.why: Theorem 3.13 is the height identity behind Proposition 2.5.1, and §§1.2.2, 3.1.3 and 3.2.5 supply the normalised Hodge divisor ξ, the point P(f_1) and the pairing f_1 ∘ f_2^∨ used in the computation. The whole reduction of Theorem B to the non-vanishing of P_K(f) rests on it.

Theorem 12.2.3, the parity theorem for Selmer groups of modular forms ordinary at λ, is used twice: to deduce ε(f,K) = −1 in Lemma 2.2.1 and ε(f) = −1 in §3. It is the only reason the sign hypothesis (sgn), required by all three of Yuan–Zhang–Zhang, Bertolini–Darmon–Prasanna and Wan, can be verified from the arithmetic hypotheses of Theorem A.

prerequisites.citation: Ralph Greenberg, "Iwasawa theory and p-adic deformations of motives", Proc. Sympos. Pure Math. 55, Part 2, Amer. Math. Soc. (1994), 193–223
prerequisites.why: §3's Panchishkin condition and §4's Selmer groups for a deformation, together with Conjecture 4.1, are the framework in which Sel_∞(f,K,S), its characteristic ideal and Conjecture 2.7.1 are formulated; §2.7 is an explicit generalisation of that setting to G_K-representations.

prerequisites.citation: Solomon Friedberg and Jeffrey Hoffstein, "Nonvanishing theorems for automorphic L-functions on GL(2)", Ann. of Math. (2) 142 (1995), no. 2, 385–423
prerequisites.why: Theorem B supplies the imaginary quadratic field K with L(f ⊗ χ_D,1) ≠ 0 and the prescribed local behaviour at 2, p and the primes dividing N; without it the choice of K in §3 and §4 cannot be made.

prerequisites.citation: Kenneth A. Ribet, "On ℓ-adic representations attached to modular forms II", Glasgow Math. J. 27 (1985), 185–194, and "On modular representations of Gal(Q̄/Q) arising from modular forms", Invent. Math. 100 (1990), no. 2, 431–476
prerequisites.why: The first gives the irreducibility of ρ̄_{f,λ} for large p and the second the level-lowering theorem from which §3 deduces that ρ̄_{f,λ} is ramified at every prime dividing N for large p; hypothesis (b) of Theorem B is verified from them.

prerequisites.citation: Jean-Pierre Serre, "Quelques applications du théorème de densité de Chebotarev", Inst. Hautes Études Sci. Publ. Math. 54 (1981), 123–201
prerequisites.why: §7.2, Corollary 2, the density zero of the set of primes with a_p(f) = 0 for a non-CM form, is what makes the set of admissible ordinary primes in §3 have density one.

prerequisites.citation: Manya Brakočević, "Anticyclotomic p-adic L-function of central critical Rankin–Selberg L-value", Int. Math. Res. Not. IMRN 2011, no. 21, 4967–5018, with Ellen Eischen, Michael Harris, Jian-Shu Li and Christopher Skinner, "p-adic L-functions for unitary groups", arXiv:1602.01776
prerequisites.why: These are what upgrade the continuous function on Γ constructed by Bertolini–Darmon–Prasanna and Brooks to an element of the Iwasawa algebra O^ur[[Γ]], by extending the interpolation to characters ramified above p. Without that the Iwasawa-theoretic argument of §2.7 cannot be stated.

prerequisites.citation: Wei Zhang, "Selmer groups and the indivisibility of Heegner points", Camb. J. Math. 2 (2014), no. 2, 191–253
prerequisites.why: The closest comparable theorem, obtained from Kolyvagin's conjecture instead: it drops the injectivity at p but requires Tamagawa factors indivisible by p. The report and the item zhang-comparison record that neither result subsumes the other; a blueprint should plan both statements separately.

prerequisites.citation: Manjul Bhargava and Christopher Skinner, "A positive proportion of elliptic curves over Q have rank one", J. Ramanujan Math. Soc. 29 (2014), no. 2, 221–242
prerequisites.why: Theorem D of this paper. It is the main consumer of Theorem B, through variations of the kind exemplified by Theorem C, and its Selmer-distribution input belongs to ArithmeticStatistics rather than here.

prerequisites.citation: Karl Rubin, "p-adic L-functions and rational points on elliptic curves with complex multiplication", Invent. Math. 107 (1992), no. 2, 323–350
prerequisites.why: Theorems 8.1 and 8.2 are the CM analogue of Theorem A, proved by a different route (Rubin's main conjecture, Perrin-Riou's p-adic Gross–Zagier formula, Bertrand's non-degeneracy); Theorem 9.5 is the CM analogue of Proposition 2.6.1, by which Remark 2.9.1(xii) says the present method also covers the CM case. The cases covered here are disjoint from Rubin's.

prerequisites.citation: Ashay Burungale, Christopher Skinner and Xin Wan, A refined non-vanishing of the p-adic logarithm of a rational point on an abelian variety, arXiv:2603.20886v2 (10 May 2026)
prerequisites.why: §1.2 identifies and repairs Skinner Lemma 2.2.2. Theorem 1.1 and Theorems 3.1–3.2 supply items 79–82. Only the unconditional rank-one algebraic-point result is needed, not §5’s higher-rank structural-rank conjecture.

prerequisites.citation: Bjorn Poonen and Michael Stoll, The Cassels–Tate pairing on polarized abelian varieties, Annals of Mathematics 150 (1999), 1109–1149; corrected author version, 23 August 2014
prerequisites.why: Public source for the Cassels elliptic pairing, Tate generalization, nondegeneracy modulo divisibility and the distinction between elliptic alternation and the general polarized case; §1 p.2 and §3. The original Cassels/Tate references are credited there; this reading is of the corrected Poonen–Stoll exposition, not a claim to have read the original proofs. Needed by 83–86 and shared with ArithmeticStatistics. Original references identified in that source: Cassels, Arithmetic on curves of genus 1, IV (1962); Tate, Duality theorems in Galois cohomology over number fields (1963).

routes.title: Rank-zero and rank-one Birch–Swinnerton-Dyer theory, Part II: the p-converse to Gross–Zagier–Kolyvagin
routes.brief:
This coalesces with the RankOneConverse Part II of RankZeroOneBSD that the maintainer routed for this very paper (DESIGN-SKINNER, issue #951, area iwasawa) and that PAPER-CASTELLA-ETAL-22 already extended with the Eisenstein-prime branch; it keeps that job's final theorems and adds the source items of Skinner, Ann. of Math. (2) 191 (2020), 329-354, itself.

Final theorems. (A) For a newform f in S_2(Gamma_0(N)) of trivial nebentypus with N squarefree, if either some odd prime l has pi_l the twist of the special representation by the unramified quadratic character, or two odd primes l_1, l_2 have pi_{l_i} special, then rank_Z A_f(Q) = [M_f:Q] together with #Sha(A_f) finite implies ord_{s=1}L(f,s) = 1; equivalently (A') for a semistable elliptic curve with non-split multiplicative reduction at one odd prime or split multiplicative reduction at two. (B) The p-adic criterion over an imaginary quadratic field K of odd discriminant with hypotheses (a)-(e), whose conclusion is ord_{s=1}L(f,K,s) = 1, rank_Z A_f(K) = [M_f:Q] = ord_{s=1}L(A_f/K,s) and Sha(A_f/K) finite. (C) The mod-p Selmer criterion Sel_p(E) = Z/pZ plus the local condition at p. (E) The analogous rank-zero statement, an alternative proof of a special case of Skinner-Urban and Wan. Theorem D of the paper, the positive proportion of curves of rank one, is a consumer owned by ArithmeticStatistics.

Import, never re-plan: RankZeroOneBSD BSD.0-BSD.4 for analytic L-functions, twists, quadratic descent, the Friedberg-Hoffstein non-vanishing and the forward Gross-Zagier-Kolyvagin direction; HeegnerPointEulerSystems HE.0-HE.1 and HE.7 for ring class fields, CM points and the classical descent; GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights GZ.0, GZ.3, GZ.8 for the normalisations and the Yuan-Zhang-Zhang height identity, and GZ.9 for the BDP/Brooks p-adic L-function and the p-adic Waldspurger formula; AutomorphicCongruences L2 for Wan's two-variable U(3,1) divisibility; ModularIwasawaMainConjectures L0 for the Greenberg/Panchishkin formulation and L1, L5 for the rank-zero converse; SelmerIwasawaCohomology L1-L4 for Bloch-Kato and Greenberg Selmer groups, duality and control; PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras L4-L5 for characteristic ideals; AutomorphicGaloisRepresentations R19.1, R19.4, R19.5 for the representation V; AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L0 for algebraic Hecke characters and their p-adic avatars; KatoEulerSystems L4 for the alternative rank-zero input.

Construct here: the two cases I and II for the pair (f,K) and the Skinner-specific epsilon_f-normalisation of the existing HE.1 Heegner points, with the cusp/Hodge/projector comparisons; the hypotheses (sqf), (sgn), (ram), (flt), (odd), (L-lrg), (big), (ord), (spl), (res), (irr), (irr_K) and the implications among them, in particular Lemma 2.8.1; the globally p-strict group and the group strict at 𝔭 and relaxed at 𝔭̄ with Lemmas 2.3.1 and 2.3.2, which is where the splitting of p in K is used; the big Galois module M = T tensor Lambda^*(Psi^{-1}), its Selmer group, characteristic ideal and Conjecture 2.7.1, stated over Lambda^ur tensor_O L as in the published version; Proposition 2.7.2 and its deduction from Wan's theorem by specialising the two-variable objects along gamma to psi_0(gamma)^{-1}gamma; the control diagram giving (2.7.1) and (2.7.2) and hence Proposition 2.7.3; and the assembly of Theorem B, the choice of the auxiliary K in section 3 and the deductions of Theorems A, C and E.

Keep the published hypotheses and coefficient rings: the arXiv preprint of 2014 places the anticyclotomic p-adic L-function in O[[Gamma]] and states Conjecture 2.7.1 and Proposition 2.7.2 in Lambda tensor Q_p, which the published version corrects (source issue E1). Wei Zhang's theorem on Kolyvagin's conjecture gives a comparable but incomparable statement, dropping the injectivity at p and adding Tamagawa hypotheses; the two should be stated separately and neither presented as subsuming the other. The historical eigendifferential-logarithm omission in Lemma 2.2.2 is repaired by Burungale–Skinner–Wan (2026), Theorem 1.1. Keep Theorems A and E under their published hypotheses, and keep Theorem B(e) explicitly. Import the proposed DT.3 analytic-subgroup and algebraic-point logarithm results (79–81) through the GZ.9 RM/Heegner application (82), passing through an actual rational divisor point before its ε_f projection. This gives no nonvanishing assertion for an arbitrary nonzero cohomology class and uses no structural-rank conjecture. Import the shared elliptic Cassels–Tate pairing, its divisible kernels, alternation and finite odd-primary paired-elementary-divisor theorem (83–86) from SelmerIwasawaCohomology L1–L2 for the assembly of C; do not assume full Sha finiteness in advance. Import the Case II curve/cohomology (87–88), quotient (89) and HE.1 points, and prove only the Skinner–Brooks normalization adapter (90) here. The published Brooks transfer normalization is §2.7; retain Skinner’s §2.8 citation as version provenance (E12). The A′ assembly (64) additionally imports R29.5–R29.6, the actual local dictionary (63) and existing elliptic isogeny invariance (91), without making modularity a converse owner. Theorem E still imports the separate derivative-nonvanishing theorem (76).
routes.reason: The maintainer routed this paper to the Part II RankOneConverse of RankZeroOneBSD (DESIGN-SKINNER), and PAPER-CASTELLA-ETAL-22 already reused that candidate for the Eisenstein-prime branch of the same p-converse; the review of PAPER-BURUNGALE-TIAN-26 asked for a single owner of the p-converse property. This route therefore reuses the same id, title and area rather than proposing anything new. The parent proves the Gross–Zagier–Kolyvagin direction at BSD.3 and BSD.4 and has no layer for the converse, and BSD.5–BSD.9 plan leading-term formulas, not a Selmer-to-analytic implication.

L4 plans the arithmetic examples and conjectures attached to Selmer groups, including the Bloch–Kato and ordinary local conditions and the statement of the Coates–Perrin-Riou/Panchishkin conjecture, but no parity theorem, and nothing else in the atlas plans one: RankZeroOneBSD BSD.0 plans only the root-number parity of the analytic order. This source adds Nekovář's parity theorem for the Selmer groups of a modular form ordinary at λ (Selmer complexes, Theorem 12.2.3), which is what forces ε(f) = −1 from a one-dimensional Selmer group in §3 and, through Lemma 2.2.1, ε(f,K) = −1 from an odd-dimensional one. It is an input quoted, not proved, in this paper, and it is the hypothesis (sgn) on which the Gross–Zagier and p-adic Gross–Zagier formulas both depend.

R19.1 constructs the weight-two representation attached to a newform with its coefficient field and lattices and R19.3 the compatible system and its purity. This source adds the three statements about the family {ρ̄_{f,λ}} that §3 needs and that no layer plans: that for a newform without complex multiplication the set of primes p with f ordinary at some λ | p has density one, which combines the Ramanujan bound with Serre's Chebotarev theorem that {p : a_p(f) = 0} has density zero; that ρ̄_{f,λ} is irreducible for all λ | p once p is large (Ribet); and that for large p it is ramified at every prime dividing N, which is deduced from Ribet's level-lowering theorem (planned at SerreWeightAndLevelOptimisation R20.2) together with the finiteness of the set of newforms of weight two and level dividing N and multiplicity one. These are statements about the compatible system as a whole, not about one member of it.

GZ.9 plans the BDP/Brooks p-adic L-function with its interpolation range, CM periods and removed Euler factors, and the p-adic Waldspurger identity at the weight-two point. This source adds the two facts about that function that Skinner's argument needs and that GZ.9 does not state. First, integrality: the functions of Bertolini–Darmon–Prasanna and of Brooks are a priori only continuous on Γ, and membership in the Iwasawa algebra O^ur[[Γ]] — without which the Iwasawa-theoretic argument of §2.7 cannot even be formulated — requires extending the interpolation formulas to characters ramified above p, as in Brakočević, or the constructions of Eischen–Harris–Li–Skinner and Wan. Second, the precise dictionary between the imprimitive L^S_𝔭(f) used here and the published L_p(f,χ): the character sets Σ^{(2)}_{cc}(𝔫) and Σ^{(2)}_{cc}(𝔫^+), the removal of the Euler factors at the primes of S not dividing p, and the identities relating C(f,χ,1), w(f,χ) and α(f,f_{GL_2})^{-1} to the constants used here. Both are comparison statements about the object GZ.9 owns. Add item 82 as a missing RM/Heegner application of Burungale–Skinner–Wan, importing the proposed DT.3 general theorem. GZ.9’s current contract does not already assert this algebraic-point nonvanishing; its warning about arbitrary cohomology classes is retained.

Added by the review. L5 plans the consequences of the ordinary main conjecture of L1 ('Prove the local Euler-factor change formulas … Define the Greenberg and Coates–Perrin-Riou conjectural generalizations'). The rank-zero converse of Skinner–Urban and Wan, that finiteness of Ш[p^∞] for one large ordinary p forces L(f,1) ≠ 0, is the standard consequence of the Selmer side of that equality, and no stage states it; the RankOneConverse brief imports it from L1 and L5.

Added by the review. ST.4 plans the Bhargava–Shankar orbit-counting Selmer theorems and their rank consequences. Theorem D (Bhargava–Skinner), a positive proportion of elliptic curves of algebraic and analytic rank one, is a rank consequence of that kind that also consumes the p-converse of this paper's Part II; the brief already names ArithmeticStatistics as its owner.

Proposed source extension for the abelian p-adic analytic subgroup theorem, its endomorphism-stable variant, and BSW Theorem 1.1. DT.3 owns transcendence/logarithmic forms but does not currently state these results. Coordinate with its partial blueprint job #1027; import the existing abelian-variety/tangent/formal-logarithm carriers, rather than duplicating them. GZ.9 imports this theorem for the modular/Heegner application and RankOneConverse imports that application. No structural-rank conjecture is required.

Proposed shared elliptic Cassels–Tate source extension: construct the pairing on the existing Sha carrier, identify both divisible kernels, prove elliptic alternation, and deduce the finite odd-primary paired-elementary-divisor theorem. Import ArithmeticGaloisDuality rather than rebuilding local/global duality. Coordinate ArithmeticStatistics.json’s existing gap “Cassels–Tate pairing and its isogeny adjointness”, needed by ST.5/three-isogeny-selmer-parity, and its L1 annihilator request. These four items do not claim to discharge the additional isogeny-adjointness request. RankOneConverse imports the shared result for 61/74. The existing L1–L2 contract has no Sha pairing theorem yet.

sourceIssues.locator: arXiv:1405.7294v1 (28 May 2014), §§2.6 and 2.7: the definition of the anticyclotomic p-adic L-function, the definition of Λ, Conjecture 2.7.1 and Proposition 2.7.2
sourceIssues.printed: The source asserts L^S_𝔭(f) ∈ O[[Γ]] for an anticyclotomic p-adic L-function with an interpolation condition for ψ ∈ Σ^c_𝔭, and defines Λ = O[[Γ]]. Conjecture 2.7.1 asserts Ch_Λ(f,K,S) = (L^S_𝔭(f)) in Λ ⊗_{Z_p} Q_p. Proposition 2.7.2 asserts, under the preceding hypotheses, Ch_Λ(f,K,S) ⊆ (L^S_𝔭(f)) in Λ ⊗_{Z_p} Q_p.
sourceIssues.correction: The published version reads: O^ur is the ring of integers of the completion of the maximal unramified extension L^ur of L; L^S_𝔭(f) ∈ O^ur[[Γ]] and the unit W of w(f,ψ) = ψ(W) lies in O^ur[[Γ]]^×; Λ = O[[Γ]] and Λ^ur = O^ur[[Γ]]; Conjecture 2.7.1 reads "Ch_Λ(f,K,S) and L^S_𝔭(f) generate the same ideal of Λ^ur ⊗_O L" and is called essentially the Iwasawa–Greenberg main conjecture; Proposition 2.7.2 reads "the ideal of Λ^ur ⊗_O L generated by Ch_Λ(f,K,S) is contained in the ideal generated by L^S_𝔭(f)".
sourceIssues.reason: The interpolation formula defining L^S_𝔭(f) has the p-adic period Ω_p^{4n} of a CM elliptic curve E_0 in it, and Ω_p is a unit of the completion of the maximal unramified extension, not of O; the same is true of the two-variable function 𝓛^{Σ,Hida}_{f_0,K,ξ} ∈ O^ur[[Γ_K]] of Wan's theorem, to which the deduction of Proposition 2.7.2 specialises. So the element L^S_𝔭(f) of the preprint's Conjecture 2.7.1 and Proposition 2.7.2 need not lie in O[[Γ]] and those two statements are not the ones the sources prove. The published version's own deduction makes this explicit: it specialises Wan's inclusion of ideals of O^ur[[Γ_K]] ⊗_O L along O^ur[[Γ_K]] → Λ^ur and concludes about ideals of Λ^ur ⊗_O L. Everything else in the preprint and the published version agrees: the 19 numbered statements carry the same numbers and, apart from these coefficient rings, the same text.
sourceIssues.known: Corrected in the published version, Ann. of Math. (2) 191 (2020), 329–354, §§2.6–2.7 (pp. 342–346), which introduces O^ur and Λ^ur and restates Conjecture 2.7.1 and Proposition 2.7.2 over Λ^ur ⊗_O L. The items of this extraction use the published form.
searched: the published PDF of the paper, open access from the Annals article page, read in full
the arXiv abstract page for 1405.7294, which lists v1 of 28 May 2014 as the only version and carries no journal reference or comment announcing a revision
the Annals article page for volume 191 (2020), issue 2, which records Revised 1 December 2019 and lists no erratum or corrigendum

review.reason: Checked in v1 (extracted text of the PDF fetched from arxiv.org/pdf/1405.7294v1: pp. 13, 15, 16) and on the published page images pp. 342–346 (p. 343 shows W ∈ O^ur[[Γ]]^×; p. 346 shows 𝓛^Σ_{f_0,𝒦,ξ} ∈ O^ur[[Γ_𝒦]]). The p-adic period Ω_p^{4n} in the interpolation formula is a unit of O^ur and in general not in L, so the v1 membership in O[[Γ]] is unjustified, as the finding says. Two qualifications. (1) The finding's claim that, apart from the coefficient rings, v1 and the published version have 'the same text' is too strong. The v1 deduction also cites 'part (2) of [26, Thm. 1.1]', '[26, §6]' and '[26, §2.11]' where the published version has '[26, Th. 1.2]', '§7.5' and '§2.2'. v1 names the function 𝓛^{Σ,Hida} rather than 𝓛^Σ. v1 says 'This is the' rather than 'This is essentially the' Iwasawa–Greenberg main conjecture. Theorem D is reworded ('A positive proportion of elliptic curves, when ordered by height, have both algebraic and analytic rank one'), and the reference numbering differs ([1]/[2] swapped; Greenberg is [8] in v1, [10] in print). (2) The 19 numbered statements do carry the same numbers.

sourceIssues.printed: The source claims the ideal generated by Ch_Λ(f,K,S) in Λ^ur ⊗_O L is consequently contained in that generated by L^S_𝔭(f). It bases this on calling O^ur[[Γ_K]] and Λ^ur unique factorization ideals and on principality of the characteristic ideals, citing [24, Cor. 3.8].
sourceIssues.correction: "unique factorization ideals" should read "unique factorization domains"
sourceIssues.reason: The property being used is that the two completed group rings are UFDs, so that an inclusion of principal ideals can be tested factor by factor after specialisation; "unique factorization ideal" is not a notion, and the reference given, Corollary 3.8 of Skinner–Urban, is the statement that these Iwasawa algebras are unique factorization domains with principal characteristic ideals. The sentence was read directly from the content stream of the published PDF, where it is unchanged from the preprint.

review.reason: Seen on the page image of p. 346. The rings are regular local rings, hence UFDs, and that is the property the argument needs. 'Unique factorization ideal' is not a notion. v1 has the same slip with O[[Γ_K]] and Λ.

sourceIssues.locator: §2.8, the proof of Lemma 2.8.1, the sentence beginning "Suppose now that", published p. 347; the same sentence is in arXiv:1405.7294v1
sourceIssues.printed: With k denoting the residue field of L, the proof assumes reducibility of ρ̄_{f,λ} over k̄. It claims the image of ρ̄_{f,λ}|_{G_K} then lies either in a split or non-split torus, or in a Borel subgroup of GL_2(k).
sourceIssues.correction: the hypothesis for contradiction must be that ρ̄_{f,λ}|_{G_K} is reducible over k̄, not that ρ̄_{f,λ} is
sourceIssues.reason: Lemma 2.8.1 asserts that (irr) and (res) imply (irr_K), so the argument must assume the failure of (irr_K) — the reducibility of the restriction to G_K — and derive a contradiction with (irr). As printed, the sentence assumes the failure of (irr) and then, four lines later, concludes "contradicting (irr)", which proves nothing. That the intended hypothesis is on the restriction is confirmed by the next sentence, which speaks only of the image of ρ̄_{f,λ}|_{G_K}, and by the dichotomy offered there: a reducible two-dimensional representation of G_K whose restriction is semisimple has image in a torus and otherwise in a Borel, which is exactly the case division the proof then makes.

The intended meaning is clear and the mathematics is right as intended. Under §18's definition ('nothing: the mathematics is right as intended') affects should therefore be 'nothing' rather than 'the proof'.

the Annals article page for 191 (2020), issue 2, which lists no erratum or corrigendum

sourceIssues.locator: §2.2, Lemma 2.2.2 and the sentence introducing it, published p. 338 (page image checked); arXiv v1 p. 9. It propagates to §3, 'By Lemma 2.2.2, hypothesis (e) of Theorem B then also holds' (p. 351), and to §4 (Theorem E, p. 352), when [M_f:Q] > 1
sourceIssues.printed: The source derives Lemma 2.2.2 from the preceding result and the freeness of A_f(K) ⊗ Q_p over M_{f,p}. The lemma asserts that rank_Z A_f(K) = [M_f : Q] together with #Ш(A_f/K)[p^∞] < ∞ imply dim_L H^1_f(K,V) = 1, with H^1_f(K,V) →res H^1(K_𝔩,V) injective for every 𝔩 | p.
sourceIssues.correction: Retain the full published Lemma 2.2.2 and Theorems A/E. Add the missing proof input: BSW Theorem 1.1 gives a nonzero logarithm in every M_f-eigendifferential for an actual non-torsion algebraic Mordell–Weil generator, since M_f is totally real and dim A_f=[M_f:Q]. Through the rational Kummer comparison and the Bloch–Kato logarithm this proves injectivity in every λ-component, for every v|p. No λ-uniqueness or additional logarithm hypothesis is needed.
sourceIssues.reason: Freeness of the global M_f⊗Q_p-module alone does not prove componentwise logarithm nonvanishing, so the printed deduction omitted an argument. historicalAssessment.correction: The dimension statement is right. The injectivity holds when λ is the only prime of M_f above p (in particular when [M_f:Q] = 1, so Theorems A′ and C are unaffected). In general it is equivalent to the non-vanishing of the λ-component of the local Kummer image, i.e. log_ω(P) ≠ 0 at 𝔩, for P spanning A_f(K)⊗Q over M_f and ω the λ-eigen 1-form. That condition must be added as a hypothesis. For [M_f:Q] > 1, Theorems A and E as proved need a prime p satisfying §3's conditions for which it holds, for example λ the unique prime of M_f above p (possible only for suitable M_f).
historicalAssessment.reason: Under the hypotheses, H^1_f(K,V_pA_f) = A_f(K)⊗Q_p = M_{f,p}·κ(P) is free of rank one. H^1_f(K_𝔩,V_pA_f) = A_f(K_𝔩)⊗Q_p ≅ Lie(A_f)(Q_p) is also free of rank one over M_{f,p} = ∏_{λ′|p}M_{f,λ′}. The restriction sends κ(P) to log(P) = (x_{λ′})_{λ′}. After ⊗_{M_{f,p}}L (projection to the λ-factor, an exact functor), the map on H^1_f(K,V) is injective iff x_λ ≠ 0. Freeness of A_f(K)⊗Q_p does not give this: P non-torsion only gives log(P) ≠ 0, not that each component is non-zero. x_λ = 0 means the M_f-line A_f(K)⊗Q lies in a proper O_{M_f}-stable p-adic analytic subgroup of A_f(K_𝔩). Excluding this is a p-adic linear-independence (Leopoldt-type) statement about p-adic logarithms, which is not known in general. The step is automatic only when the λ-factor is all of M_{f,p}. The same point is why Theorem B asks for injectivity as part of (e), and why the atlas's GZ.9 warns not to infer a non-zero logarithm from a non-zero class.
